#3116. Can you still trust Proton?

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The company’s reputation took a major hit two weeks ago, when 404 Media published a detailed report, based on leaked Slack messages and interviews with anonymous insiders. The story detailed a push by Proton CEO Andy Yen to — in his own words — “ruthlessly smash everything that stands in the way of AI velocity.”

Also: Is your browser’s free VPN enough? I tested 4 against Proton VPN

After one employee proposed spending at least a few days on penetration testing before shipping new code, Yen reportedly said, “That’s bullshit and loser thinking. Of course it’s possible to be fast and secure. Stop thinking always of how to be slower, and focus more on how to be faster.” According to 404 Media’s account, Yen’s message for Proton engineers was to “stop lovingly handcrafting all our code and use AI more.”

After the original story broke, 404 Media posted a follow-up story reporting that the company had canceled its “re-interviews” that were intended to assess how developers were adopting AI. A 404 Media podcast was titled “Proton’s CEO Is Putting AI Before Security.”

Reddit has an especially active Proton community with 345,000 weekly visitors. It quickly filled up with so many comments — the majority of them negative — that moderators created a single megathread to help keep track of the different threads, including pages for general criticism, support of the AI usage, and “leaving your goodbyes.”

Also: Best VPN services 2026: Expert tested and recommended

Given the level of interest, it’s not surprising that Yen chose that forum to post a public message to the community. In it, he apologized for “hurtful” remarks, adding that he’s “determined to do better.”

He also addressed the topic of AI-based security reviews:

But most importantly, I need to categorically state that our use of AI will never be at the expense of security. In the past year, contrary to what has been alleged, actually additional layers of security review have been added to meet the threat posed by hostile AIs scanning Proton’s open source code for vulnerabilities. Fast and secure need not be mutually exclusive. We also leverage AI to find vulnerabilities in our own code before attackers do. Our code is open source, and its security remains open for all to verify. [emphasis in original]

Nothing in the 404 Media reporting demonstrates that Proton weakened its encryption or shipped insecure code because of AI. The damage is different: Yen’s remarks undermined confidence that management will consistently respect the security processes its customers rely on.

In a blog post that Proton shared with ZDNET ahead of its publication today, the company followed up on Yen’s promise to “lift the hood on how we use AI internally at Proton.” The post, titled “How Proton keeps your data secure in the age of AI,” was signed by the Proton Team and emphasizes Proton’s secure architecture, with end-to-end, zero-access encryption:

We do not hold the keys to your emails, files, or passwords, so we cannot read them, and no AI tool can, either. Our documented security governance policies have not changed since June 2024, before AI was even a major factor in our work here, and they all still apply.

On Reddit, Yen said, “AI is here, and it will unquestionably change how software is developed forever, and Proton must also change.” Today’s post clarified that code receives the same checks whether it is written by a human, by an AI agent, or by a combination of both. Every change receives automated security scans but also requires human approval; sensitive changes, such as core cryptography work, require review by specialist teams. Major feature designs are also reviewed for security, dependencies, testing, and deployment plans.

Also: I can access my home PCs remotely for free – no VPN needed

Those policies address the most serious technical concerns raised by the current controversy, although outsiders have no way to know from the policy alone how consistently those safeguards are followed in day-to-day development.

Should a modern software company use AI for security? Proton argues that it can’t afford not to.

Because of AI, attacks that once might have required a nation-state can now be executed by almost anyone. A defender relying on manual processes and hand-crafted tools is bringing a knife to a gunfight. An attacker only needs to find one flaw, while a defender needs to close all of them. AI is the only tool that makes that defense possible. Cybersecurity is an arms race, and the teams working on security at Proton have been some of the earliest adopters of AI, because the safety of your data depends on winning that race.

But that argument doesn’t really address the objection. The current controversy isn’t about whether Proton should use AI to find vulnerabilities; it’s about whether pressure for “AI velocity” can override the judgment of engineers responsible for keeping its products secure.

Proton says it uses AI to review code changes, identify vulnerabilities through continuous security reviews, and monitor an attack surface that has “grown far beyond what unaided humans could monitor.” The company uses its own models alongside non-public cyber models from OpenAI and Anthropic.

The modern software development landscape is torn by two opposing forces. On one side, you have AI-based tools that are routinely finding nightmarish vulnerabilities in existing codebases and then exploiting them immediately. On the other side, you have a global movement that’s skeptical of the benefits of AI and outright opposed to construction of the data centers where they run.

Much of Proton’s growth over the past few years has been the direct result of people trying to escape big tech. So it shouldn’t be a surprise that many of Proton’s customers — at least those who are passionate enough to visit a Reddit forum — are deeply skeptical of anything related to AI.

Also: Ring’s new drone patrols your home to keep an eye on things – even upstairs

In a traditional software company, that realization would have led management to cautiously roll out AI-based features and reveal its AI-centric security strategy more deliberately. That didn’t happen here, obviously. Those blunt remarks from the CEO exposed a management culture that many employees and customers found troubling. It’s difficult to restore trust, both within the workforce and among customers, after that kind of public display of contempt.

Ironically, one of Yen’s comments from the original 404 Media story describes the company’s current dilemma with devastating accuracy.

In a Slack message, Yen told a Proton engineer, “perception is more important than truth, the truth doesn’t matter if you don’t win on perception.” The implication was that he was urging the employee to lie, or at least shade the truth. In fact, as Yen himself told a random Reddit commenter:

I do not believe perception should be more important than truth. I am stating that unfortunately it often ends up being the case. If you place it into the context in which it was said, it can be understood as, “it doesn’t matter that the truth is that Proton’s PQC implementation is better, this truth is irrelevant as long as it is not perceived to be this way, and we therefore need to correct that perception”

That’s Proton’s challenge now, distilled to its essence. It takes seconds to destroy a reputation. It can take months or years to recover from the perception that the company and its management can no longer be trusted.

Personally, I will continue to use Proton Pass and Proton VPN, both of which are solid, reliable products. But I’ve moved my secondary email accounts (which I had migrated from Gmail to Proton Mail); they’re now running on Fastmail. I had been considering making the switch for a long time, primarily because Proton Mail’s performance has been too slow for my taste. Current events just hastened that switch.

#3114. How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain – and what you can do

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

New research provides a stark look at the AI supply chain and the risks it brings to businesses.

Artificial intelligence companies worldwide are bringing a new wave of vulnerabilities and security issues to the digital supply chain, researchers warn.

According to a new report published by Black Kite on Tuesday, there now exists a “widespread cybersecurity weakness” across the “rapidly expanding ecosystem of companies developing, deploying, and supporting artificial intelligence.”

AI and smart solutions don’t automatically equate with safe solutions. In a study titled “2026 AI Supply Chain Report: The Risks Behind Your AI Relationships,” Black Kite says that many AI suppliers — the companies that develop and deploy AI services to today’s businesses — are struggling with “basic security practices.”

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

According to the research, after examining the companies themselves, along with their software, integrations, and components, researchers found failures to patch critical vulnerabilities, protect credentials, authenticate users and email, and address network security issues.

The study analyzes 18,160 AI companies worldwide, ranging from 0-10 employees to more than 1,000 employees. A company’s AI involvement was determined through reviews of company products and services and primary business activities, covering six broad groups: everyday application development; AI development and implementation; AI applications in specialized sectors such as healthcare, IT, and finance; industrial organizations; and AI foundations working on data, compute, and modeling.

A small percentage of assessed companies are considered “unclassified,” and the study excluded businesses that use AI only incidentally.

In addition, unusual network activity was detected at 44.3% of organizations, and botnet-related activity was recorded at 41.8% of AI companies.

AI’s main business appeal is its ability to integrate with existing software and platforms to handle manual tasks, heavy lifting, and tedious, time-consuming work, freeing employees to focus on work that requires human oversight.

Enterprises are investing billions of dollars in AI. Menlo’s 2026 research estimates that enterprise AI spend reached $37 billion in 2025, with half of overall spend going to AI apps. In total, 76% of enterprise AI solutions are purchased rather than built internally.

However, the moment an AI or automated component is introduced into a corporate ecosystem or operational platform, any security problems it has impact the user — and each additional integration, such as software components or open-source tooling, may also increase the attack surface.

In an accompanying analysis of AI firms’ use of Model Context Protocol (MCP) components, which can link AI apps to business systems, 48.8% of 1,732 logged security findings were rated High or Critical, including code and command injection vulnerabilities.

Also: The new enterprise AI expert every company needs

It’s not just the AI application itself. As noted by Black Kite, AI suppliers often have access to customer data, developer environments, business infrastructure, and enterprise platforms. If the supplier’s credentials are stolen, this could expose its customers to a range of cyberattacks.

The researchers found, for example, that 19.9% of AI companies offering solutions for enterprise AI deployment had corporate login information in infostealer records, and that stolen corporate logins, overall, were linked to 6.8% of AI suppliers in the study.

Visibility matters, too, for businesses that should be monitoring their digital supply chains. However, 33.2% of AI companies assessed have a “limited” digital footprint, including their domains, subdomains, and IP addresses.

The same principles for protecting the digital supply chain apply to AI suppliers, where continual monitoring and assessment are among the best protections businesses have.

Staying informed and aware of the risks to your own business makes all the difference. As recommended by Black Kite, it takes more than a single point-in-time security assessment — frequent monitoring and engaging with suppliers to understand their technologies and dependencies can reveal potential security issues.

Also: Do you need AI agent liability insurance?

If you find weaknesses, manage them by priority, handling ransomware-related exposures and vulnerabilities actively exploited in the wild first.

Also audit an AI tool’s integrations and components, access, what data it can reach, and the potential impact of exploitation. Once you’re armed with this information, it’s possible to weigh risk and reward — and whether the AI tool is worth the potential attack exposure it brings. If you decide to keep it, limit its permissions and access to what it requires.

#3112. Ring’s new drone patrols your home to keep an eye on things – even upstairs

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home & Office > Smart Home > Home Security

Alongside the Ring Drone Cam, Ring introduced the Rover Cam for businesses. It investigates disturbances and streams 4K footage.

Today, Ring announced the launch of a new subbrand, Ring Robotics, with two new products: the $249 Ring Drone Cam, an indoor “mobile security camera” drone that shoots 2K video, and the $999 Ring Rover Cam, a security robot for businesses that patrols autonomously and investigates disturbances.

Also: Amazon’s new Echo Studio gives Alexa+ an AI camera to see inside your home

Both devices use Ring’s custom navigation software, “AI Pilot,” to autonomously navigate interior spaces and move between set points along a patrol, rather than being controlled directly by the user. AI Pilot leverages the devices’ cameras, sensors, and vision models, along with cloud processing, to create interior maps, then move the devices between predesignated patrol points such as a side door or a window.

I recently saw both new robots in person at a showcase in New York hosted by Ring’s founder and chief inventor, Jamie Siminoff. They certainly do what they advertise but come with some significant limitations. The drone, for example, can only stay in the air for about 8 minutes before it needs to dock and recharge, while the Ring Rover Cam is slow and deliberate, seemingly ideal for routine surveillance rather than rapid response to an event.

The Ring Drone Cam moves around predetermined patrol points in your home, sending you a live 2K video feed whether you’re just in another room or out of town. The user doesn’t actually fly the drone; instead, it moves around autonomously using Ring’s custom “AI Pilot” navigation technology, leveraging its cameras, sensors, and cloud processing to create a map of its surroundings. This allows it to fly through the air at an appropriate height, going from room to room, even up stairs.

In the Ring app, the user creates patrol points they want the drone to move between — likely a window, doorway, or high-traffic room — creating a set path that is both predictable (so you always know where the drone will go) and relevant, so it’s only monitoring the areas you want it to. But here is where its limitations come into play: It needs a finite path to navigate because its flight time is limited to just five to eight minutes in the air before it has to return to its charging dock.

That makes the dock both the start and end point for the drone’s routine trips, and it’s designed with this in mind. When it goes to land, the drone hovers over the dock and lowers itself down, dropping into place so it can start charging automatically. I asked about its potential to land elsewhere, and Ring told me it would only make an emergency landing outside of its dock in case it didn’t have enough power to get home.

Also: Amazon’s new Echo Dot can turn into a Wi-Fi extender – how it works

There’s one other very important caveat: This thing is loud. There’s no sneaking up on anyone with the Ring Drone Cam, as the entire household is likely to hear it the second it undocks. The four propellers emit a constant, high-pitched whirring while in the air that’s loud enough to announce its presence to anyone in the vicinity: intruder or resident.

During the product briefing, Siminoff insinuated that this was part of its design to dissuade home intruders snooping around your house at night (especially when paired with the drone’s front-facing spotlight), but it’s likely just the result of its engineering, especially considering this is a first-gen product. It’s so loud that it makes me think it’s better suited to navigating the home when no one’s home (although whether or not your pets go bonkers trying to catch it is a whole other issue).

The Ring Drone is designed to work out of the box with the existing Ring ecosystem, including the 2K Video Doorbell and Indoor Cam, and is also compatible with Amazon’s Map View.

The Ring Drone Cam will start shipping on Jan. 27, 2027, and will cost $249.

The other product Ring announced is the Rover Cam, a mobile robot with a 4K camera designed to monitor large spaces like warehouses, offices, or businesses. Ring calls it a “security guard that never clocks out,” but it’s more like a slow-moving droid that goes on set patrol paths. It leverages the same AI Pilot technology as the Ring Drone to map its surroundings and navigate around shelving, furniture, and obstacles in real time.

It’s much quieter than its airborne sibling, traveling at low speeds and offering mobile surveillance instead of wiring every square inch of a large space. If the technology here looks familiar, it’s because it resembles the Amazon Astra, a smaller robot designed for home monitoring but with a very similar build.

The idea here is to deploy the robot to certain areas of a workplace via the app, then get 360-degree views once it’s there. Like the drone, it can also set out on automated routes at select timing intervals — like right after a business closes or before it opens. During working hours, it chugs along with its camera, capturing everything in its view.

Also: The 4 biggest Amazon smart home announcements from today

If another Ring device is triggered, the Rover Cam autonomously goes to investigate the disturbance, providing 4K footage in real time via the app. It also features a periscope camera that can extend to see over obstacles like shelving, counters, or furniture, providing a high-level view if needed. In case you lose it in a large warehouse or office, it has a “light tower” that projects light upward onto the ceiling, notifying users of its location.

Even when docked, it uses motion-sensing technology to start recording the second it senses any kind of movement, just like Ring doorbell cameras. In case of an emergency, the Rover features a siren and red flashing lights to dissuade intruders.

The Ring Rover Cam is available for preorder now and will start shipping on Dec. 16, 2026. It will cost $999.

#3110. 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home & Office > Smart Home > Smart Assistants

With the latest betas for iOS and other platforms, Siri AI is now available to all developers for full integration into their apps. Here are the ones I hope will jump on board.

One of the many benefits of the new Siri AI is its ability to work directly with apps on your device via a feature known as App Intents. Currently, this skill includes many of Apple’s own built-in apps and some third-party ones. But with the latest public and developer betas for iOS 27.3, the company is expanding support to all third-party developers.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade

With App Intents, you’re able to ask Siri to tackle a variety of actions among various built-in and third-party apps. On a basic level, you can tell it to perform tasks such as getting directions, playing music, scheduling meetings, sending messages, adding reminders, and finding photos.

On a more advanced level, you can ask it to do things like organize your inbox, edit a photo, and analyze and help you with your current screen. You could also tell it to combine several actions in one shot, work across multiple apps, and engage in a natural back-and-forth conversation.

Introduced in 2022 with iOS 16, the App Intents skill does play well with classic Siri, no Apple Intelligence required. This applies not just to built-in apps but also to third-party apps. However, classic Siri lacks the AI smarts and advanced skills of the latest version.

Siri AI fully supports most built-in apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. It does support some third-party apps, but its more advanced features are limited or unavailable.

That’s the gap the new developer betas aim to close. With iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, MacOS 27.3, and VisionOS 27.3, all developers will be able to use Siri AI to fully support and integrate with their apps. For example, instead of manually opening an app like DoorDash or Grubhub to check or change a food order, you can tell Siri to do it for you.

Also: The Siri AI waitlist is gone in iOS 27: How to try the beta now

“Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, on-screen awareness, natural language, and more,” Apple said in a news release for developers. “So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.”

As I use many third-party apps on my iPhone and iPad, both personally and professionally, I’m looking forward to enhanced support for the ones I rely on. With that in mind, here are five apps for which I’d welcome the new and full Siri AI integration.

I often use Amazon on my iPhone and iPad to shop for and purchase items, review my wishlist, and check the status of products I’ve ordered. To do any of those things, I have to open the app and manually go to the right screens. How convenient it would be if I could tell Siri to handle those tasks for me.

“Siri, search for the 512GB 2026 iPad mini on Amazon and add it to my shopping cart.”

“Siri, review my Amazon wishlist for the luggage I recently added and tell me the latest prices.”

“Siri, check the delivery status of the Alexa photo frame I just ordered on Amazon.”

Right now, Siri can’t do any of those things. But if Siri AI and App intents are fully integrated with Amazon, I may just be able to accomplish those tasks in the future.

IMDB is my go-to app for getting info on movies, TV shows, performers, directors, and more. After I open the app and run a search, I often want specific details, such as the rating and runtime of a particular film or TV episode.

Also: AI completely changed how I develop iPhone apps

To simplify that process, I’ve love to be able to ask Siri: “Siri, search IMDB for the 1935 movie ‘The Bride of Frankenstein,’ give me the running time, tell me where I can stream it, and add it to my watchlist.” If Siri could accomplish all that at some point, it would get a round of applause from me.

I borrow and read a lot of e-books through my local library systems, and I use the handy Libby app for that. Here, I can search different libraries for books by title, author, or subject. I can then borrow a book and read it through the Libby app or, more typically, through the Amazon Kindle app. For this, I have to manually open the app and search among the various libraries for the book I want.

Also: I lost 100 pounds in 7 months: How a smart scale and Apple Watch helped

Instead, I’d like to ask Siri to do that for me. I might say: “Siri, look in Libby for books about Alan Turing, give me the titles of the ones you find, and tell me which ones are currently available to borrow.”

My wife and I are big theater buffs, and we see a lot of plays on Broadway when we’re in New York and on the West End when we’re in London. Often, I buy tickets through the TodayTix service and app. For this, I’ll open the app, set the location to New York or London, look for a specific play, and then try to find seats for a certain day and time.

If TodayTix is ever fully supported by Siri AI and App Intents, I might be able to ask Siri to track down the right seats for me. I could say: “Siri, look for the play ‘Rent’ in London, give me the available performances for Dec. 5 through 9, and let me know which seats are accessible in the first 10 rows.”

As my wife and I often travel and dine out, Yelp is another app I frequently use. Here, I also have to manually launch the app and run searches for restaurants and other places. I then have to try to filter or sort the results based on location, price, and ratings.

Also: 3 handy iPhone features that make my life easier – even doing laundry

Asking Siri to tackle those tasks would certainly be a time saver. I could ask it to “find the closest Italian restaurants using Yelp and show me ones within a one-mile radius that have earned four stars or higher.”

With App Intents, Siri AI can already handle advanced, complex, multi-step tasks for built-in apps. With all developers now able to take advantage of this same support, I’m expecting a lot of apps to jump on board. Let’s hope my favorites end up on the list.

#3109. Intercorp Financial (IFS) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Consumer lending surged despite El Nino provisions weighing on profit.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Intercorp Financial Services Inc. (IFS +1.38%) reported third-quarter results characterized by growth in higher-yielding loan segments and the continued scaling of its digital payments ecosystem. Management maintained its full-year profitability guidance while taking a proactive approach to risk management through extraordinary provisioning for climate-related contingencies. The company reported a recovery in net interest margins, driven by a shift toward consumer and small business lending and a reduction in funding costs. Operations were supported by a resilient macroeconomic environment in Peru, where private investment and domestic demand reached multiyear highs. The company continues to prioritize its digital transformation, reporting high penetration across its banking, insurance, and wealth management platforms.

They will be discussing the results that were distributed by the company yesterday. There is also a webcast video presentation to accompany the discussion during this call. Otherwise, if you need any assistance today, please call InspIR Group in New York on (646) 940-8843. I would like to remind you that today's call is for investors and analysts only. Therefore, questions from the media will not be taken. Please be advised that forward-looking statements may be made during this conference call. As such, statements made are based on several assumptions and factors that could change, causing actual results to materially differ from the current expectations. For a complete note on forward-looking statements, please refer to the earnings presentation and report issued yesterday.

It is now my pleasure to turn the call over to Mr. Luis Felipe Castellanos, Chief Executive Officer of Intercorp Financial Services, for his opening remarks. Mr. Castellanos, please go ahead, sir.

Luis Castellanos López-Torres: Thank you. Good morning, and thank you all for joining us on our third quarter 2026 earnings call. Let me start with the macro environment. In the first half of 2026, private investment grew 15%, its fastest growth since 2012, and domestic demand grew almost 6%, which is the highest since 2013. Exports have reached new historical records, and all of this has come with a prudent fiscal deficit and debt-to-GDP ratio. Business confidence is also at its highest level in recent years. On the political front, we see the executive pushing forward its investment agenda, which is consistent with expectations for a stronger private investment and should help bring Peru back to its medium-term growth potential.

All in all, we are optimistic about what lies ahead for Peru, and we believe the coming years should be positive. In the short-term, we are especially focused on the El Nino event, which we are now assuming that will be an extraordinary magnitude. We expect that impact to be temporary, mainly affecting primary sectors such as agriculture and fishing and -- extending into the first half of 2027. Depending on the strength of the rains, infrastructure primarily in certain regions of the North will be affected. Even so, we continue to expect GDP growth of around 3% next year. We believe the country is well-positioned to return to its medium-term growth path once these effects fade.

In this context, IFS net income was PEN 457 million with an ROE of 14%. These results mainly reflect the provisions that were booked in anticipation of El Nino at Interbank and to a lower extent at SIP, in line with our prudent approach to risk management. Excluding these provisions, net income would have been PEN 543 million with an ROE of close to 17%. As mentioned, we see the impact of El Nino as short-term, while our medium-term view has actually improved. We see our medium-term ROE target to be above 20% now. At Interbank, the underlying business continued to show positive trends. Excluding El Nino provisions, risk-adjusted NIM expanded to 3.9% from 3.5% last quarter.

Loan growth accelerated in consumer and in small businesses, both higher-yielding segments, which is contributing to the NIM expansion. Asset quality is also performing very well with a positive trend. Year-to-date cost of risk, excluding El Nino provisions, is 1.8% and NPLs is at 2%, reflecting the quality of our portfolio and our risk management capabilities. As a result, we believe the bank is better positioned as we enter this El Nino period as compared to the previous ones. We continue to strengthen our payments ecosystem through Izipay and PLIN. These platforms are important levers to deepen our relationships, increase engagement, and support the growth of low-cost funding.

Interseguro maintained strong momentum in its core business while preserving its leadership in annuities. The business continues to leverage synergies with Inteligo and Interbank to advance more integrated solutions for our customers. Inteligo continued to grow at double-digit rate, reaching a new record in assets under management, supported by healthy client engagement and strong advisory model. The investment portfolio had more moderate quarter, but this does not change the trend of its core business. Overall, this quarter shows that we remain on-track in terms of results and profitability, supported by a diversified platform, clear growth opportunities across businesses and a disciplined execution of our model. El Nino event should be a short-term effect.

Our strategy remains focused on profitable growth with the customer at the center of our decisions and continued investments in the capabilities that support long-term value creation, including digital solutions, data analytics, cybersecurity, and GenAI. Looking ahead, we believe IFS is well-positioned to continue growing with discipline while sustaining profitability and strengthening our leadership in Peru over the long term. Now let me pass it on to Michela, who will walk you through this quarter results in more detail. Thank you.

Michela Ramat: Thank you, Luis Felipe. Good morning, and welcome again, everybody, to Intercorp Financial Services' Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. I would like to begin with our key messages for the quarter. First, Peru remains resilient ahead of El Nino. Even after incorporating a stronger El Nino, the Central Bank projects GDP growth of 3% for 2027. Second, core earnings maintained a positive growth trajectory. Excluding El Nino-related provisions, net income was PEN 544 million with an ROE of around 17%. Third, accelerating momentum in higher-yielding loans, which grew 21% year-over-year and 10% in the quarter alone. Fourth, NIM recovery on a better asset mix.

NIM expanded 20 basis points to 5.1% and risk-adjusted NIM, excluding El Nino provisions, improved 40 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 3.9%. Finally, insurance and wealth management continued to deliver strong growth with written premiums up 30% in the first 9 months and assets under management up 13% year-over-year. Let's start with our first key message, which is that Peru remains resilient ahead of El Nino. On Slide 4, let me update you on the macro environment. The economy is regaining speed. GDP is tracking around 3.4% in the third quarter based on data through August, up from 2.6% in the previous quarter. Nonprimary sectors continue to support growth.

The Central Bank now expects GDP to grow 3.2% this year and 3% in 2027, below its previous estimates of 3.4% and 3.2%, as it incorporates a stronger El Nino. Growth remains supported by commerce, services, and construction, with exports at record levels. Looking ahead to 2027, we expect a more challenging first half as El Nino would weigh on activity during the summer months. However, we anticipate a significant recovery in the second half, supported by reconstruction spending and the fiscal response. The impact will not be the same everywhere.

The North, the most exposed region, would contract in the first half and rebound in the second, while other regions would be less affected, limiting the impact on overall annual growth. Inflation reached 5.3% in October, remaining above the Central Bank's target range. Core inflation is lower at 4.6%. And excluding transportation, which was affected by fuel prices increases, it would be close to 2%, consistent with the target range. That said, the reference rate has remained at 4.25% over the past year and a rate increase over the next 6 months cannot be ruled out. Overall, Peru continues to stand out for the strength of its macroeconomic fundamentals. Public debt remains among the lowest in Latin America.

Country risk is one of the lowest in the region, and financing conditions remain favorable across the yield curve, supporting a constructive medium-term outlook. On Slide 5. For a bank, what matters is whether this macro recovery translates into credit demand, and we are beginning to see clear signs that it does. Business confidence rose to 69, its highest level in recent years, while consumer confidence reached 50 points. This improving sentiment is translating into stronger spending in investment decisions. In fact, the Central Bank expects domestic demand to grow 6.2% this year and private investment 14%, one of its strongest expansions in more than a decade, with private investment remaining resilient at 8.5% in 2027.

Supporting this outlook is a robust investment pipeline for 2026-2030, totaling USD 124 billion. Mining represents 52% of the total and infrastructure, another 28%, led by projects such as Tia Maria, Trapiche, Pampa de Pongo, Anillo Vial Periferico, de la Sierra Tramo 4. Beyond their direct impact, these projects should continue supporting employment, business activity and financing needs across sectors. We can already see this momentum in the financial system. As of September, loans grew 11.8% year-over-year with retail expanding 13.8%. We are seeing a similar trend in our own portfolio, which reinforces our view that renewed confidence is translating into stronger credit demand. On Slide 6, before turning to the results, let me spend a moment on El Nino.

ENFEN's October update raised the probability of an extraordinary cost at El Nino in the first quarter of 2027 to 55% from 9% in June. So we are facing the possibility of an extraordinary event, and therefore, we decided to provision in line with this scenario. Around 11% of our loan portfolio is flagged as potentially exposed with about 8% through direct exposure to agriculture and fishing, which we consider very low risk, and about 3% through consumer and small business loans in the affected zones, which we consider medium risk. The 8% is made up entirely of commercial clients with direct exposure and all of them already have sent clauses that allow them to refinance or defer payments.

So we do not expect the agriculture and fishing exposure to generate provisions for the bank. On the 3%, retail clients do not have these clauses, which is why we see it as medium risk, but we are ready to support them through rescheduling programs allowed by the superintendency. This quarter, Interbank set aside PEN 185 million in total provisions for El Nino, comprising PEN 81 million of already held under expert criteria and PEN 104 million of additional provisions. SIP recorded PEN 37 million as well, of which 50% or PEN 18.5 million was recognized by IFS. Including our share of SIP, the after-tax impact on IFS net income was PEN 86 million.

This provisioning reflects the scenario we see today, which assumes a stronger El Nino than previously expected, but we will reassess as the event evolves. We are already acting by tracking the exposed portfolio on a daily basis, tightening underwriting standards in the affected areas and supporting our employees in those areas. Once the event has passed, we will be there to support recovery in the affected regions. On the government side, the Ministry of Economy has announced a broad support package that includes additional fiscal funding, cash transfers to affected families, state-backed loan guarantees for SMEs and accelerated public work programs.

Together with reconstruction spending, these measures should help mitigate the economic impact of El Nino and support a stronger recovery in the second half of 2027. Let's now turn to our second key message, which is that core earnings maintained a positive growth trajectory. On Slide 8, in the context of what we just discussed, our core earnings are on the right track. Excluding El Nino-related provisions, net income was PEN 544 million, up 19% year-over-year with an ROE of 16.6%. Compared to last quarter, net income was down 7%, mainly because investment results at Inteligo and Interseguro normalized after a strong second quarter.

Once we include the El Nino provisions at Interbank and SIP, reported net income was PEN 457 million with an ROE of 14%. Overall, setting El Nino aside, the underlying trends remain solid year-over-year and the bank is leading the way. At the bank, the net income, excluding El Nino was PEN 439 million, up 10% from last year and 9% from last quarter, with an ROE of 16.4%. This was driven by higher loan income and lower funding costs, which are also behind the NIM recovery. At Interseguro, net income was PEN 97 million with an ROE above 30%.

That's below an exceptionally strong second quarter, but 2.6x what we reported a year ago when the results included a credit loss provision on financial investments. At Inteligo, net income was PEN 38 million with an ROE of 13.5% as investments return normalized after a very good first half of the year. Importantly, the recurring part of the business is on-track, and fees and assets under management continue to grow. On Slide 9. Looking at the first 9 months of the year, net income excluding El Nino was PEN 1,731 million, up 17% year-over-year with an ROE of 18.1%. Including El Nino, reported net income was PEN 1,644 million, up 11% year-over-year with an ROE of 17.2%.

The important point is that even after absorbing El Nino, we remain in line with our full year ROE guidance of around 17%. On Slide 10, revenues grew 8% year-over-year to PEN 2.1 billion and flat versus the previous quarter. At the bank, the trend is encouraging. Revenues were up 4% in the quarter and 8% year-over-year with NIM recovering to 5.1%, in line with our strategy to grow in higher-yielding loans. We also benefited from lower funding costs, partly offset by lower FX results. At Interseguro and Inteligo, revenues declined versus the previous quarter by 3% and 30%, respectively, due to investment results, which were very strong in the previous quarter.

The underlying trend is moving in the right direction as revenues grew 12% year-over-year at Interseguro, driven by the insurance result and 8% at Inteligo. On Slide 11. Expenses for the first 9 months grew 10% year-over-year, and our cost-to-income ratio was 37.8% compared with around 37% a year ago. The main driver was technology, up 15% versus last year as we continue to invest in cybersecurity, infrastructure, and data and analytics. Personnel expenses are up 14%, reflecting the expansion of Interseguro sales force and key talent that we are adding across the platform. Now let's turn to our third key message, which makes us most optimistic about the coming quarters. On Slide 13.

Our higher-yielding loans, consumer and small businesses are accelerating, growing 21% year-over-year and 10% in the quarter, almost doubling the pace of the previous quarter. In consumer loans, the recovery we anticipated in our last two calls is now materializing. Excess liquidity is normalizing and activity is coming back, supported by better confidence. As a result, consumer loans are up 18% year-over-year and 10% in the quarter, outperforming the market and gaining 20 basis points of market share versus last quarter. In September, cash loan disbursements grew 44% year-over-year and credit card turnover 21%. And so far, we have not seen a pause due to El Nino.

In small businesses, growth continues at an accelerated pace with loans up 34% year-over-year and disbursements up 63% in September. Our business banking app, which brings together Interbank and Izipay, the acquiring business, strengthens our value proposition, and we still see room to continue gaining share. Together, these segments now represent 23% of the performing loan book, which supports NIM recovery. That said, these segments are also the most sensitive to El Nino. So we want to be very clear that we are growing conservatively. We are focusing our growth on zones that we do not expect to be affected by El Nino and on low-risk clients and we have already tightened origination in the exposed areas. On Slide 14.

Our performing loan book grew at a double-digit pace or 10% year-over-year, up from 6% last quarter. In the quarter alone, it grew 4% with good momentum in both retail and commercial. What we like about this growth is that it is broad-based and led by segments with attractive risk-adjusted returns. Starting with retail, we are growing more than 9% year-over-year. Consumer, as previously mentioned, is leading with 18%, and mortgages continue to grow steadily at 8%. The good news is that now mass market is the fastest-growing segment at more than 10%, while the affluent segment is growing as well, but at a more moderate pace. In commercial, we are growing 11%, led by small businesses at 34%.

And I would also highlight midsized companies, which are growing more than 14%. Deepening our relationships and complementing our value proposition with Izipay is helping us grow both in small businesses and midsized companies. Turning to our fourth key message, a NIM recovery on a better asset mix. On Slide 16. The NIM story is positive, and it is driven by lower funding costs and a better asset mix with a higher weight of loans that should keep building in the coming quarters. NIM increased 20 basis points to 5.1% with contributions from both assets and funding. On the asset side, the return on interest-earning assets rose 20 basis points to 7.7%.

Importantly, this came mainly from loan yields, which rose to 9.7%. This marks a change in trend driven by the shift towards consumer and small business loans, which now represent 23% of the performing loan book. At the same time, our asset mix is improving with loans now representing close to 70% of the interest-earning assets. Excluding El Nino provisions, risk-adjusted NIM was 3.9%, which is 40 basis points above last quarter, reflecting our strategy to grow in higher-yielding loans. Including El Nino provisions, it was 3.4%. Looking ahead, we expect the shift in mix towards higher-yielding loans to become a larger driver of NIM together with lower funding costs.

Given the possibility that the Central Bank raises rates, it is worth sharing our sensitivity. For every 100 basis points increase in the soles reference rate, we estimate a negative impact of around 7 basis points on NIM. On Slide 17. Excluding El Nino, cost of risk was 1.9%, below the 2.1% of both last quarter and a year ago. Including it, cost of risk was 2.7%, so El Nino explains the entire increase. The underlying indicators all improved. Delinquencies are declining mainly due to better payment behavior of customers, in line with stronger economic activity. Our recent vintages are also performing well across the portfolio, even with the growth we mentioned in higher-yielding loans.

In retail, excluding El Nino, cost of risk was 3.4%, slightly above the 3.3% of last quarter. That increase reflects the growth of the portfolio. Commercial remained very low at 0.5%, which, together with an NPL ratio of 1.3% shows the portfolio is performing well. El Nino provisions were booked based on expert judgment as we decided to provision for the scenario we see today. We will reassess as the event evolves. Excluding El Nino, we would expect a slight increase in line with portfolio growth in higher-yielding segments while continuing to improve risk-adjusted returns. On Slide 18. The improvement in funding is the other half of the NIM story.

Cost of funds fell 10 basis points in the quarter and 20 basis points from a year ago. This is a result of the mix, which is moving in the right direction as low funding costs increased to 39% of total funding, reflecting our focus on the payments ecosystem, primary banking and transactional deposits. Retail and commercial deposits now represent 85% of funding and the loan-to-deposit ratio is at 93%. On Slide 19, our payments ecosystem connects directly with the funding trends we just discussed. More transactional activity brings more low-cost deposits and creates cross-selling opportunities. In payments, flow from the Interbank Izipay relationships grew 58% year-over-year and Interbank's share of Izipay flows increased to 48%.

In small business, deposits grew 30% alongside 34% growth in loans. Engagement continues to rise. PLIN transactions are up 43% year-over-year and 86% of our retail customers are now digital, which is the engine behind our lower cost of funds. PLIN also keeps expanding its use cases. PLIN TC or PLIN credit cards, which lets customers send money using their credit card line, has already surpassed 100,000 active customers. On WhatsApp, we cut transactions time by 1/3 and transactions per user increased by 17%, reflecting stronger customer engagement and higher recurrence. We are also making the app more useful and safer with tools like Modo Calle, which helps reduce fraud from phone theft.

Clients are noticing with retail NPS reaching 64 points. We are growing while improving the customer experience, which makes that growth sustainable. Let's now turn to our fifth key message on insurance and wealth management, where growth remains healthy. On Slide 21. At Interseguro, the key metric is the contractual service margin, or CSM, which represents the stock of future profits from our long-term insurance business. It reached PEN 1.2 billion, up 8% year-over-year, driven by annuities and individual life, and short-term insurance grew 10% year-over-year. Investment results were PEN 278 million, a 6.6% return, well above last year's 4%, when we recorded credit loss charges on financial investments.

Compared with last quarter, the return is broadly stable, excluding inflation effects. The 7.1% return in the second quarter would have been 6.7%, very much in line with this quarter. Overall, the business is performing well as expected. On Slide 22. At Inteligo, assets under management, including deposits, reached USD 10.1 billion, up 13% year-over-year, supported by market performance and net inflows from clients. Fee income reached PEN 53 million, up 5% year-over-year and 3% in the quarter. This is the recurring part of the business, and it continues to grow alongside assets under management. Overall, Wealth Management continues to deliver resilient growth, supported by a strong advisory model and healthy demand for investment solutions. On Slide 23.

We are bringing the same digital approach to insurance and wealth management. At Interseguro, direct digital sales grew 25% year-over-year to PEN 40 million and 74% of client interactions are now self-service, improving both customer experience and cost to serve. At Interfondos, we are turning the app into a digital adviser. Digital users went from 30% to 42% of customers in a year, supported by accelerated app adoption, which added more than 11,000 new clients versus the same quarter last year. Digital transactions now represent 64% of platform activity, up from 55% last year, while physical transactions continue to decline. Our renewed website and richer content also strengthened our digital ecosystem.

Now let me move to the final part of the presentation, where we bring everything together. On Slide 25. Let me bring together what we have discussed on growth. Our growth is broad-based with retail loans up 9% year-over-year and commercial loans up 11%. Within the bank, our focus is on consumer and small businesses, and this is where growth is accelerating with consumer loans, excluding payroll deductible loans up 18% and small business loans up 34% year-over-year. Beyond the bank, long-term insurance and wealth management keep growing with the CSM of insurance up 8% and assets under management up 13% year-over-year. On Slide 26.

I'd like to close with our 9-month operating trends and how they compare with what we commented at the beginning of the year. On profitability, ROE for the first 9 months is 18.1%, excluding El Nino, or 17.2% on a reported basis. We continue to expect a full year ROE of around 17%, even after absorbing El Nino provisions. On loans, growth is 10% year-over-year, a little bit above the high single-digit growth we expect for the full year. The acceleration in higher-yielding segments gives us confidence. On efficiency, our cost-to-income ratio is around 37%, within our guidance range even as we continue to invest for growth. Let me close the presentation with our key takeaways.

First, Peru remains resilient ahead of El Nino. Second, core earnings maintained a positive growth trajectory. Third, we are accelerating and we have a momentum in higher-yielding loans. Fourth, NIM recovery on a better asset mix. Finally, insurance and wealth management continued to deliver strong growth. Thank you very much. Now we are ready and welcome any questions you might have.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] The first audio question will come from Ernesto Gabilondo with Bank of America.

Ernesto María Gabilondo Márquez: My first question will be on El Nino. So you mentioned that total exposure to El Nino represents roughly 11% of your total loan book. So just wondering how much additional provisions would you require in the fourth quarter and maybe in the first quarter of next year? Luis Castellanos López-Torres: Ernesto, thanks very much. Yes, you're right. The other 3% potentially exposed is more in consumer and SMEs, also mentioned by Michela. Based on the scenarios we're running and as was mentioned, we're running -- today, we know it's going to be an extraordinary El Nino event. That's what we are considering in our numbers.

So with the information that we have now, that's the level of provisions that we consider we will have. As Michela mentioned, we need to continue monitoring because news continue to change. But if we do have an extraordinary El Nino, as has been mentioned and analyzed during the last couple of months by the analysts, this is what we should have. If conditions change, maybe we, like, overbook provisions if it's not as strong or if something happens that becomes stronger than extraordinary, probably have to reassess at that time. Ernesto María Gabilondo Márquez: Okay. Michela Ramat: Thank you, Luis Felipe. Good morning, Ernesto. Yuri, talking about funding, as you see from the slide, cost of funds was down 10 basis points in the quarter, but also cost of deposits was 10 basis points below the previous quarter. There are a number of reasons, but I would say that the main one is what Luis Felipe mentioned. We continue to grow faster on the low-cost funding elements on the funding base, which comes from retail deposits, transactional deposits, but also small business and midsized companies deposits, which are nonremunerated. So those components are growing double digit and faster than the rest of the funding base.

There was also a small impact because of the -- what you mentioned, the double carry of the bond that -- starting the full October, we don't have. That also helped. But I guess the more medium-term trend is what I mentioned about the strategy. Now of course, going forward, we have some pressure on cost of funds because of what is happening with rates. So we are trying to balance those two forces. Now talking about capital. You described the situation perfectly. And one of the things that kind of changed in the OCI is the non-realized losses that the previous quarter were non-realized gains on the portfolio of sovereign bonds that we have at the bank, okay?

Now just to remind you about our internal policy for both core equity tier 1 and total capital ratio. There are new regulatory limits that go fully in place December 2026 that for Interbank are around 9% core equity tier 1 minimum capital ratio and around 14.2% total capital ratio, okay? So with the levels that you see, we are okay, we are comfortable and we are above our internal buffers. It is important to mention also that with this new regulation in place from the superintendency, there is a much broader differentiation, if you want, in terms of the capital requirements for the different banks in the system.

And that I think is important because as the systemic buffer is different among banks, you will also see minimum regulatory requirements, which are very different between us and the other top banks in the country, okay? In our case, we are in the first bucket of that buffer, which is 50 basis points. But in the case of other banks, that goes up to 150 basis points to 200 basis points. So I think it's important to consider that you will start to see different total capital ratios in the system, but also because the minimum regulatory requirements have a difference of around 150 basis points, okay? So now in any case, we are growing faster than expected.

So we continue to assess our plan -- our medium-term plan in terms of funding. We have more space in the core equity tier 1. As you can see, we are a little bit tighter in the total capital ratio. So we are, of course, in any case, looking at our strategy for 2027.

Luis Castellanos López-Torres: And just to round up, you're right, we completed our approved buyback program, I think, at the beginning of last year or at some point last year. So we completed that program. We have purchased equivalent to around $200 million of IFS shares equivalent. And...

Carlos Tori Grande: Sorry, Luis. I just wanted to complement Michela on the funding part. She explained like the reason for the growth. But what's behind it is the strategy with Izipay and PLIN. As we grow the flows from Izipay, that brings funding, and same with PLIN, we're growing 40%, 50% per year on PLIN transactions, and that translates in more funding. So that's kind of the -- when we speak about the strategy is working, I think that's where it starts. And then obviously, the NPS and everything that we're building in our app helps with the funding.

Yuri Fernandes: No. Great. Super clear answers. If I may, just a final follow-up on the buybacks. You completed the program. Any plans of opening new programs on buybacks?

Luis Castellanos López-Torres: Yes. That's being reviewed right now. Yuri, as you know, we have a positive view on the potential evolution of the shares. So management is ready to recommend that, but we have to balance growth, liquidity to capital as well. So that has not been defined yet, but it's an alternative that we will definitely evaluate at the right time.

Yuri Fernandes: And liquidity, right? Sometimes people ask about the share liquidity as well.

Luis Castellanos López-Torres: Liquidity -- the good thing is that liquidity has improved significantly even after the buybacks. We used to trade, like, as I call it, by appointment. And today, we see like $10 million to $15 million of average daily trading volume in NYSE. So that has come back a long way during the last, I'd say, 3 years.

Operator: The next question will come from Carlos Gomez with HSBC.

Carlos Gomez-Lopez: I have two. And like Yuri, I want to move beyond El Nino. So the first one refers to PLIN. It's obvious that as a platform, it is running behind its competitor today. I mean, this can change in the future. What can you do to make PLIN more competitive in the market? And where do you see this kind of business going forward? And second, more generally, as a management team, you have a public profile, you write in the newspapers. We have a new administration. We have the prospect of stability in government over the next 5 years. What is it that we should be looking for?

What -- are you excited about in terms of changes that we can see with this administration? And what could worry you if it doesn't happen?

Luis Castellanos López-Torres: Sure. For your strategic question, I would like to pass it on to Carlos, who I'm sure can give you a little bit more detail on exactly how we see this.

Carlos Tori Grande: Thank you, Luis Felipe. Hello, Carlos. So on PLIN, the first thing that's important to understand is when you talk about the competitor, I'm assuming you're speaking about Yape. And it's very important to understand that we're not comparing apples-to-apples, right? PLIN is a brand and it's, let's call it, a highway through which payments go through. It's not an app. It's not a separate app. It's not a transaction. So when we talk about PLIN vis-a-vis Yape, most of the things that we do at Interbank, PLIN helps all the other things that we do at Interbank.

For example, the micro loans that Michela mentioned through PLIN TC, that's not something that you're going to see when we speak about PLIN. It's something that you see at the Interbank app, right? When we pay services, you see it in Interbank. When we do digital loans, we see it in Interbank. So what PLIN has helped us with is a lot of engagement and growth in terms of transactions and the -- how deep our relationship with our clients are, but you don't see everything when we talk about PLIN. In terms of transactions, Yape has grown a lot, and they are definitely larger than PLIN.

But our growth over the last couple of years has been 40% in the last 12 months and almost 100% the year before. So we continue to grow. We continue to have deposits coming from this strategy, and we're looking to accelerate constantly. Probably, what's coming in from the Central Bank with TAPP, which is somewhat similar to Pix, is going to be an accelerator, not necessarily for PLIN, but for Interbank and new customers coming in and more transactions. For example, anything we do through TAPP will not be PLIN, but will be Interbank, it's the same customer. So I would say we are very bullish in terms of the next few quarters in terms of payments.

Luis Castellanos López-Torres: Does that answer your question, Carlos?

And then one thing that I forgot to mention, and it's very important, there's a lot of growth coming in from SIP. Luis Castellanos López-Torres: Thank you, Carlos. Just to add, like, probably based on what Carlos was mentioning, it's more like apples-to-apples view will be Yape to SIP than Yape to PLIN. And that growth is the way to go around the economy in order to reduce the gaps that the social landscape of Peru has. So that's kind of the overall understanding. #3108. Google Introduces 3 More Top-Level Domain Names, Including .Eat and .Fly

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Prospective website owners can now register domains geared toward food, travel and local bands.

We’re trained to type .com almost on autopilot, but more top-level domains are coming. You’ll soon see websites ending in .eat, .fly and .here. It’s a new way for restaurants, travel agencies and other service providers to customize their online presence.

Google successfully filed these domain types with ICANN, the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers, back in 2012, but only released the new registry options to the public on Tuesday.

There’s always a concern that someone will steal a business’ domain name, a process known as cybersquatting. To prevent new top-level domains from being registered and ransomed at high prices, Google’s partnered registrars offered .eat, .fly and .here websites to registered trademark holders ahead of a wider rollout. This closed access period lasted from Sept. 1 to Nov. 9.

Google’s blog post about the new domains revealed several big businesses that have already secured new web addresses during the trademark holder selloff. Wingstop bought up wingstop.eat, while agriculture and food-tech company Clayton Farms secured the america.eat address. Caddy, Canary and Voltair are some of the businesses with new .fly domains.

The most interesting assortment of companies have tied down .here addresses. In its blog, Google describes .here domains as denoting businesses “where people get things done.” They utilize fairly common words that people might search for. Real-estate app Zillow owns rent.here and sell.here, while bloodtest.here is owned by SiPhox Health, a home blood-testing service.

A number of Google-partnered registrars are now accepting registrations for the three new domain types.

There’s currently a one-time early registration fee associated with registering the new domain names, though it is diminishing and will completely disappear on Nov. 17. After that, any currently unused .eat, .fly and .here names can be registered and maintained at a fixed annual rate, just like any other type of domain.

A representative for Google didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

#3106. Reddit launches AI-powered Reviews feature – with 10,000 products to start

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Reddit is adding AI-generated product reviews that compile real user sentiment from across communities. Here's how they work.

If you regularly turn to Reddit for product advice, your experience is about to change.

Reddit announced a new feature on Tuesday called Reddit Reviews, which takes conversations from subreddits across the site and compiles them into AI-generated, in-depth product summaries. The feature works much like Google AI Overviews and is likely an attempt to better compete with them.

When you search for a product on Reddit, you’ll see an “easy-to-digest format” that has a “what people are saying” recap. A visual breakdown will show whether conversations are generally positive, mixed, or negative, as well as common sentiments among users. If you want to go deeper, Reddit says you can browse comments about a product, apply topic filters, read original user discussions, ask follow-up questions, or explore other commonly compared products.

In an example shared by Reddit, a user searches for “Best headphones 2026.” The search returns several results with tags like “Very positive,” “Positive,” and “Mixed.” Clicking on one expands to a review that says, “Reddit likes the XL224’s fantastic battery life, powerful bass, and strong sound quality, while the steep price and fit on smaller heads draws criticism.”

“A mix of generative AI and other in-house technology” is used to identify themes and summarize what people are saying, a representative explained, and added that “the technologies and models we use may evolve over time to best support the experience.”

Perhaps the most important part is that Reddit Reviews are shaped by users, and companies can’t pay to have product features. For a community sensitive to commercialization, this is a big deal.

My first concern was about bots or other fake reviews, but a Reddit representative said they’re taking that into consideration. “Platform-wide,” the representative said, “we are labeling apps and prompting accounts we detect to be running automations to either verify there’s a human behind the username or be labeled as an app.” In this context, an app is a registered API client that’s developed to interact with Reddit (including posting, commenting, upvoting, and scraping). In short, the system will label known bots.

Also: Ring’s new drone patrols your home to keep watch – even upstairsSpecifically for reviews, a “review conversation” will appear that describes a person’s experience with a product. Reddit also has “defined rules,” it says, “to help our LLMs identify these review conversations based on the surrounding conversation for context.”

You’ll start to see Reddit Reviews over the next few weeks in the US on iOS, Android, and browser versions of the site. Around 10,000 products across electronics, health and beauty, home and garden, and fashion and apparel will be available to start.

I find myself frequently adding “reddit” to Google searches for everything from the best restaurants in a city to the best headphones for my kids, so these overviews are definitely intriguing. It’s not easy right now to wade through numerous threads, so if this does make it easier to get true user sentiment, it could be a big plus.

#3105. BlackRock's Rick Rieder sees 'historic' opportunity in high-quality bonds

Investors may be wary of the volatility hitting parts of the bond market right now, but they have an "historic" opportunity to grab attractive yields in high-quality credit, Rick Rieder, BlackRock's chief investment officer for global fixed income, told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

Hypothetically, it's now possible for investors to build a diversified portfolio that yields more than 7% with less than three years of duration and an average credit quality of A-, he said. Duration is a measurement of a bond's price sensitivity to fluctuations in rates, and issues with shorter maturities tend to have lower duration.

"Not only is it historic in that these yields are where they are, but the only time these yields are ever here is when there's some problem, like an economic problem or default problem," Rieder said in an interview about his fourth-quarter outlook, released Wednesday.

That isn't the case now, where the economy remains strong, he said. "So you don't really have to worry about defaults of any significance."

While Rieder didn't specifically identify the credits in the aforementioned portfolio, the iShares Aaa - A Rated Corporate Bond ETF (QLTA) has a 30-day SEC yield of 5.68% and an effective duration of 6.48 years — higher than Rieder's low duration focus.

The iShares Flexible Income Active ETF (BINC), which is managed by Rieder, has a 5.66% 30-day SEC yield and three-year effective duration, but its portfolio extends beyond investment-grade credit.

Rieder sees the best opportunity right now in investment-grade corporate bonds — which he pointed out he hasn't said "in a really long time." Investment grade bonds are rated AAA through BBB- by S&P and Fitch, while Moody's rates them Aaa through Baa3.

That includes hyperscaler bonds, which have flooded the market with issuance this year as they ramp up their AI infrastructure. Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms and Oracle have issued a total of about $228.4 billion in bonds year to date, as of Oct. 20, according to LSEG.

"They're very low leverage. They have tremendous amounts of cash flow coming in," Rieder said of the hyperscalers in general. "You're now getting to buy these entities which are higher quality, paying you a very attractive yield to get it."

Rieder's iShares Flexible Income Active ETF has upped its allocation to investment-grade corporates to 14.3% of its portfolio. In July, that stood at 8.5%.

That said, investors need to be patient and sit tight since rates could still move higher from here, he advised.

"Your starting point is by far your best barometer of what your return is going to be," he noted. "So if you get seven and a quarter, maybe you get eight, maybe you get six, but ... if your holding period is a year or longer, you're going to get that yield."

Caution should also be exercised outside of investment-grade credit, which requires more selectivity and deep research, he warned. That includes AI names.

"There's parts of the data center supply that's not hyperscaler guaranteed or hyperscaler backed," he said. "That we've been more cautious around, and we'll continue to be."

The bond market, particularly high-yield credit, has been rocked as investor concern grows over the massive amount of debt some companies are taking out to fund their artificial intelligence build-out.

Junk-rated CoreWeave has become the poster child, seeing its stock drop, bond yields jump and credit-default spreads widen. Oracle, which is sitting in the lower end of investment grade and is seen as a bellwether on the broader AI market, has also taken some hits.

Rieder is also keeping an eye on the Federal Reserve, which is expected to raise its federal funds rate again in December to combat inflation. The market is currently pricing in a nearly 90% probability that the central bank will hike at that time, according to the CME Group FedWatch tool.

The money manager expects that to happen, although he does not agree with it. Higher rates are hurting parts of the economy, like housing, while not having much of an impact on other areas — such as tech companies' capital expenditures, which have become a big driver of growth, he said.

"They're not borrowing off the overnight funds rate," Rieder noted. "There's a lot of floating rate finance in housing, credit card, auto loan finance, and you're seeing those areas already under pressure."

Instead, the market is and will continue to price the AI supply coming into the market, he added.

Rieder sees a number of possible risks ahead, including rising levels of government debt across the globe. In the United States, the budget deficit has grown to $2 trillion for fiscal 2026.

"The more the central banks raise the rates, the cost of debt to these to already indebted governments is something we've got to be careful about over time," he said.

Bond supply coming from AI companies should also be watched.

"With the amount of supply that's coming — data center, hyperscaler — there's some crowding-out effect that's taking place," he said. "With government rates moving higher, that is something that we just got to keep an eye on."

In the meantime, Rieder would just continue to reap the rewards of high investment-grade yields "and smile a lot," he said.
