With that, I would now like to turn the call over to Vincent Capone, Spectral AI's Chief Executive Officer. Vincent, please go ahead.

Vincent Stanley Capone: Thanks, David. And thank you all for joining us today. We issued our earnings release this afternoon which contains additional details of our operating results and we will be filing our 10 Q with the SEC on or before November 16 of this year. Our third quarter results reflect the continued transition of Spectral AI from a research and development organization into a commercial enterprise. Commercialization of a new medical technology requires more than regulatory authorization. It requires establishing clinical confidence expanding our existing relationships with leading burn centers, demonstrating economic value to hospital systems and ultimately integrating this technology into the clinical workflow. These are precisely the areas where our team is focused. We are making good progress.

With the initial BARDA supported deployments of our DeepView AI system for our first commercial sales which remain an achievable goal for 2026. To that end, during this quarter, we began manufacturing the first 30 DeepView AI systems for BARDA supported deployments at US burn centers. We are encouraged by the engagement we are receiving from burn centers across the country and the progress being made toward expanding our national sales footprint. We believe that clinical infrastructure, relationships and evidence we are building today are essential to establishing a sustainable and expanding commercial business. Our vision extends beyond simply placing devices in hospitals or burn centers for mass casualty preparedness.

While preparedness remains an important component of our strategy, we believe the much greater opportunity is to make this technology available as part of the clinical protocol for everyday burn care. We want to establish a national sales footprint for our DeepView AI system that supports more consistent objective, and timely burn wound assessments with the ultimate goal of improving patient outcomes. We believe patients should have access to the benefits of our advanced diagnostic technology regardless of where they live, where they are burned, or which burn center they visit. We are focused on making this technology broadly accessible to patients regardless of the geographic location, or socioeconomic status.

With a goal of helping ensure more equitable access to advanced burn wound assessment and the highest quality of care. As part of this strategy, we have started clinical studies in The United States and The United Kingdom. In The United Kingdom, we are self funding a study to expand our label to include head, hands, and feet burn areas. We have completed all site initiation visits at 4 burn centers in The United Kingdom. And have currently enrolled 10 patients in this label expansion study. In The United States, to further support the economic development, of our DeepView AI system.

We are finalizing preparations for our Triage and Treatment ALKENS study, or as we like to call it, the TNT study. Which will evaluate DeepView AI's potential to improve surgical precision, accelerate treatment decisions, and reduce hospital length of stay. We expect to commence the TNT study at 4 to 5 burn centers in early December of this year. With plans to expand to 12 centers across The United States by the end of the first quarter of 27. As we work through our commercialization model, we recognize the economic value of reimbursement.

To both hospital systems and the physicians themselves, we have been working hard to create a heightened reimbursement coding for the use of our device in both inpatient and outpatient settings. Early in the third quarter, we submitted a new technology add on payment or NTAP application to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services for our Deep View system. If approved, this would provide hospitals with additional Medicare reimbursement for eligible use of the Deep View system, helping to reduce adoption barriers for both eligible health systems as well as making it easier to integrate and utilize our device in the appropriate inpatient setting. We expect the determination to be made by August of next year.

On the physician side, we note that our reimbursement pathway has been advanced as of 01/01/2027. With pricing supported by local Medicare administrative contractor pricing. Our CPT 3 coding, we are working to move to a CPT 1 coding, which will be supported by our TNT study. We are also continuing to expand the total body surface area burn calculation that uses our DeepView systems imaging and AI platform to quickly and objectively quantify how much of a patient's body is burned. The advancements we are working on will provide a standardized data driven input for triage, fluid resuscitation, and treatment decisions which are especially valuable in complex or mass casualty situations.

In connection with our international sales strategies, we are still progressing with updating our UKCA burn assessment approval which we secured in 2024, to reflect the improved algorithm, hardware, and software that was included in our FDA clearance just this past May. Although we had anticipated receiving clearance by year end, we now expect this approval in early 27 after which time we will commence initial sales and placements of the DeepView AI system in either The UK, Australia, or the Gulf Cooperation Council countries. We believe our existing relationships with leading global burn centers, will also support the initial commercial launch. Outside of The United States, to date, we have made good progress.

Regarding awareness, we are encouraged by our interactions at the Southern Regional Burn Conference in September where leading burn surgeons presented new study results involving our DeepView AI system. Those presentations address physician accuracy, in identifying non healing burns as well as the repeatability and reproducibility of the DeepView Systems AI analysis. Furthermore, in October, we showcased the DeepView AI system at the American College of Emergency Physicians Scientific Assembly in Chicago. This provided yet another opportunity to introduce our technology and discuss its potential role in burn assessment and hear directly from emergency physicians about their clinical needs and how our device supports those requirements.

While the economics of our development work are different from those associated with the commercial business we are building, We remain well capitalized to execute on our strategic commercial priorities. We ended the quarter with more than $11 million in cash, a manageable debt profile, and access to an additional $90 million of nondilutive funding from BARDA. As we make this transition from a research organization to a commercial focused enterprise, we remain disciplined about how we will deploy capital and how we will fund our business and its growth. Our immediate priorities are clear. Complete initial manufacturing and begin the initial BARDA-supported sale deliveries of the DeepView AI system across a national footprint.

Further advance our commercial sales efforts both domestically and internationally with existing relationships, leading to initial sales across both The U.S. And abroad, We wish to continue to support clinicians as they evaluate and introduce DeepView AI in its clinical workflow, and to continue our reimbursement and label expansion initiatives To support hospitals and physicians. With that, I am pleased to turn the call over to David McGuire, our Chief Financial Officer.

David McGuire: Thanks, Vincent. Before I walk through the numbers, some context on where we are with BARDA. BARDA has supported the development of DeepView AI with a $250 million of non dilutive funding and that work led to FDA de novo authorization in May. In June, we completed the phase of our current BARDA contract and moved into its follow on development phase In this phase, the scope narrows to specific development projects and the costs are shared. BARDA reimburses a portion of our development costs and we fund the rest. The third quarter was our first full quarter under this phase. And as we noted last quarter, we prepared for it.

Research and development revenue for Q3 26 was $2.9 million down 24.7% from $3.8 million in Q3 25. BARDA revenue was $2.7 million compared to $3.4 million reflecting this narrower scope and the cost share. Revenue from other U. S. Government programs principally the MTEC Handheld Devin Program was $100 thousand compared to $400 thousand as work under that program was completed. Gross margin was 27.2% compared to 42.7% reflecting our share of development costs with BARDA which is recorded in cost of revenue. Total operating expenses for Q3 26 declined 4% to $4.7 million from $5 million in Q3 25.

While we continue to invest in our commercialization activities, we are managing costs carefully without compromising our ability to execute Breaking OpEx down by category in Q3 26, compared to Q3 25, R&D expense increased to $2 million from $1.5 million primarily from The U. The airline’s newest lounge will be the second-largest in the network, offering flyers an upgraded experience at Dulles.

You’ll no longer have to go to the basement to get into a United Club at Washington Dulles International Airport.

The brand-new United Club in the new IAD Concourse E spans nearly 40,000 square feet across an upstairs floor and can seat 630 passengers, making it a significant upgrade to the carrier’s existing lounge portfolio at the airport. It’s the second-largest United Club after its newest lounge in Houston, which opened just weeks earlier.

The new lounge by gates E14 and E16 opens to customers Nov. 10, 2026. United invited me to a media preview of the lounge, and here’s what you can expect inside.

The lounge features several nods to D.C.’s iconic landmarks and monuments, as well as the region’s natural beauty.

When you first enter the lounge, you’ll need to scan your boarding pass and then head up the escalators (stairs and elevators are also available) to get to the lounge.

One of my favorite design features as a former D.C. resident is that escalator ride up, which has been recreated to feel like you’re inside a Metro station.

Thankfully, the escalator ride is not as long as at some stations. Looking at you, Dupont Circle!

Once you're upstairs, you’ll walk into the heart of the lounge, with two buffet stations, a centerpiece bar and plenty of seating options, whether you’re traveling as a group or by yourself. (More on food and beverage options later.)

It’s impossible to miss the soaring ceilings in this lounge, especially compared to the bunker-like atmosphere at some of the existing United Clubs.

Don’t forget to look up, where you’ll see a cherry blossom sculpture, an homage to one of the region’s most popular attractions.

There are also two additional lounging areas on both sides of the central area. One is inspired by the Blue Ridge Mountains, which you can see in the distance.

The other has a cherry blossom theme, with light fixtures that branch out from the ceiling.

Massive windows run throughout the lounge, allowing in tons of natural light and offering fantastic views of the airfield. United has a major presence at IAD, so expect to see plenty of United planes.

The United Club has a full kitchen, allowing it to offer upgraded food options compared to its existing lounges at IAD.

You can expect to find sandwiches, salads and hot protein dishes. The lounge also had a ramen bar and a chili bar set up during my visit.

The two buffet stations are located right next to each other, with a dessert station in between.

If you want something to drink, you can head to the bar or one of the hydration stations throughout the space.

There’s plenty of seating at the bar, which has a double archway design. There are also large TVs if you’re trying to keep up with one of Washington’s many sports teams.

The United Club has eight phone booths for those who need to make a call. They’re split between the two lounging areas in the club.

You'll also find a single-stall private restroom, a wellness room, and dedicated men’s and women’s restrooms.

There are no showers in this lounge. To access a shower in a United lounge, you’ll need to head to the Polaris Lounge, reserved exclusively for eligible business class passengers flying on United and select partner airlines.

You can access the United Club by holding elite status, a lounge membership, the right credit card or an eligible premium cabin ticket.

If there’s availability, United sells day passes at the door for flights departing within three hours. You’ll also need a valid same-day boarding pass on a United or Star Alliance flight.

Holding the right credit card is probably the easiest way to get in. United’s most high-end card comes with a United Club membership, while others might offer one-time passes.

If you’re looking for a United lounge, the newest club in Concourse E is where you want to be. It offers more space, lots of light and elevated food options compared to other United Clubs.

Its massive footprint could also ease overcrowding, a common complaint with other lounges.

One thing to consider is location. The concourses at IAD are spread out, and you may need to take a mobile lounge or train to get there. If you want to check out the lounge, make sure you give yourself enough time to get to your gate.

#3064. Bionano Genomics (BNGO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Flow cell sales hit a quarterly record as supply constraints kept back orders elevated.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Bionano Genomics, Inc. (BNGO +6.03%) reported financial performance for the third quarter of 2026, highlighting a strategic transition toward profitable growth through the routine clinical adoption of optical genome mapping. Management stated that the company is prioritizing high-volume users and menu expansion to drive recurring consumable revenue. The company is working toward achieving adjusted EBITDA neutrality by the end of 2027, supported by cost discipline and planned improvements in supply chain capacity. Developments in reimbursement, including a proposed Medicare coverage determination and new Category 1 CPT codes, were identified as primary drivers for future market penetration.

Operator: Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to Bionano Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Conference Call. [Operator Instructions]. Please be advised that today's conference call is being recorded. I would now like to hand the conference over to your first speaker today, Webb Campbell, Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Webb Campbell: Thank you, Stephanie, and good afternoon, everyone. Welcome to Bionano's Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Conference Call. On the call with me today are Al Luderer, Chairman and Interim CEO of Bionano; and Mark Adamchak, Bionano's Chief Accounting Officer. After market closed today, Bionano issued a press release announcing its financial results for the third quarter 2026. A copy of the release can be found on the Investor Relations page of the company's website. Certain statements made during this conference call may be forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially from such statements due to several risk factors and risks, some of which are identified in Bionano's press release and Bionano's reports filed with the SEC.

These forward-looking statements are based on information available to Bionano today, November 10, 2026, and the company assumes no obligation to update statements as circumstances change. During our call, we may refer to certain non-GAAP financial measures, which we believe provide useful information for investors. Reconciliations of these measures to GAAP can be found in our press release and slide deck. An audio recording and webcast replay for today's conference call will also be available online on the Investor Relations page of the company website. With that, I will turn the call over to Al.

Albert Luderer: Thank you, Webb, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to be here with you all today to share our third quarter 2026 results. Bionano delivered a strong third quarter. Our results reflect the trust our routine use customer base places on our products and the continued global utilization of optical genome mapping, or OGM, for discovering and analyzing diseases. Over the quarter, we saw momentum build across our business as well as the broader genomics community. Clinical adoption is what drives our results, and we saw progress on several fronts that make it easier for customers to bring OGM into routine practice.

We expect that adoption, along with greater use at both existing and new clinical sites to remain the foundation of our growth moving forward. We continue to pursue our mission of transforming pathology, the field devoted to understanding the causes, progression and impact of disease. Traditional methods for structural variant detection are costly, repetitive, labor-intensive and time-consuming. By helping customers move to digital workflows supported by our consolidated platforms, automation and decision intelligence software, we can provide a faster, more efficient and more informative way to analyze the genome. Today, I'll walk through how we have been advancing toward that goal across our 4 strategic pillars.

I'd like to take a moment to revisit the framework that guides how we execute. In September 2024, we made a deliberate shift away from aggressive installed base growth towards profitable growth with our existing routine users. By placing an emphasis on prospects most likely to become routine, high-volume users, we've positioned ourselves to be a more focused, agile and sustainable company. In practice, this is done through the following: first, to support and sustain our installed base of routine OGM and VIA software users; second, to increase OGM utilization by routine users by supporting menu expansion and improving ease of use with VIA and Ionic adoption.

Third, to build the support needed for OGM reimbursement and inclusion in medical society guidelines and recommendations. And fourth, to improve profitability and scalability through lower costs, higher volumes and continuous improvement in product quality. So turning to our first and second pillars, which are focused on supporting our installed base and driving greater utilization of our products. Q3 2026 flow cells sold were up 18% year-over-year at 9,870 units, a record for any quarter. In short, our customers are processing more samples than ever and a large share of that added volume comes from laboratories bringing OGM into routine use.

Now breaking down our revenue segments, Consumable revenue was $4.7 million in Q3 2026, up 24% year-over-year, driven by sales to existing customers in the Americas. Software revenue was $1.1 million in Q3 2026, down 31% year-over-year, reflecting a lower number of VIA software licenses sold in the period. Other revenue, which includes instruments and services, was $2.5 million in Q3 2026, up 24% year-over-year, led by higher instrument sales to new customers. The continued move towards more recurring consumable-driven revenue gives us a healthier and more predictable business and is evidence of our strategy in action. I'd also like to highlight the geographic profile of our quarter.

Revenues in Europe, the Middle East and Africa grew 14% year-over-year to $4.1 million, up from $3.6 million a year ago, driven by growth in instrument revenue. Revenue in the Americas grew 35% year-over-year to $3.8 million. Adoption of OGM is not happening in a vacuum. Its value is being recognized globally as the investments we have made in evidence generation begin to translate to adoption.

Regarding our second pillar, increasing OGM utilization by supporting software adoption and menu expansion, customers continue to give us very positive feedback on our software and compute upgrades that let them broaden their test menus and run more samples and in some cases, have allowed them to double weekly cancer sample throughput with no change to their hardware. Our VIA software remains the gold standard for CNV analysis on microarrays, and we continue to see adoption among NGS and long-read sequencing labs. Customers who use VA without OGM give us a base of software revenue, and this is often the first step towards using more of our platform.

Ionic, our system for producing high-purity DNA and RNA also remains a key focus, supporting both OGM and NGS workflows at scale. We are increasingly seeing our software offerings as an on-ramp to broader OGM platform adoption. As we begin to see the transition of array via customers to OGM, we will eventually recognize some decline in software revenue, but expect to offset this loss by bringing these customers deeper into our OGM ecosystem. As we focus our resources on the largest opportunities in clinical OGM, we view the migration of these customers to OGM as a critical step forward for more routine use. Now highlighting our third pillar, building support for OGM reimbursement and inclusion in medical society guidelines.

An important development this quarter was MolDX's proposed local coverage determination or LCD for OGM. In late August, MolDX published a proposed LCD that would set Medicare coverage in the Medicare administrator contractor jurisdictions that follow MolDX, representing 31 U.S. states. This coverage determination establishes a criteria for OGM-based genome-wide detection of copy number alterations and structural variants in hematologic neoplasms. The public comment period has now closed, and we look forward to the final determination. Today, Medicare is the largest payer for cancer care and about 60% of new cancer diagnoses are in Medicare eligible patients. MolDX states also represent roughly 61% of the U.S. population and private insurers often write their policies in line with Medicare coverage.

For laboratories, a clear coverage pathway lowers the financial risk of validating OGM and moving it into routine use, further supporting the broader adoption and utilization that drives demand for our products. This builds on the reimbursement foundation we described last quarter. As we previously noted, the AMA has approved 2 Category 1 CPT codes for OGM, one in hematologic malignancies and another for constitutional genetic disorders. Additionally, CMS has established reimbursement rates for both codes. The coverage determination from MolDX would add a clear path to Medicare coverage for OGM and hematologic malignancies. Together, we believe these developments are creating meaningful momentum for OGM and make it easier for customers to become routine users.

Another milestone this quarter came in New York, where 2 leading academic centers are now bringing OGM into their clinical laboratories. The New York State Department of Health approved OGM-based laboratory developed tests at University of Rochester Medicine, covering genetic disorders, reproductive disorders and hematologic malignancies. Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center then launched OGM-based hematologic malignancy testing following state approval. State approval is a significant step allowing institutions to offer OGM testing in New York. As more leading cancer centers adopt OGM in their clinical workflows, our base of routine users expands, subsequently driving utilization of our products.

Now expanding on our third pillar, the growing body of evidence continued this quarter with 3 new independent peer-reviewed publications showing the potential clinical value of OGM in high-risk myeloid cancers. The first published in modern pathology by researchers at MD Anderson used OGM to study 332 samples from subjects with myelodysplastic syndromes or MDS. OGM identified chromoanagenesis, a catastrophic single event genomic restructuring process in 15.9% of cases overall and 17.6% of newly diagnosed subjects. These subjects had a median survival of 9.9 months, while the median survival for the rest of this group was much higher as it had not been reached during the study.

Researchers noted that this information could help doctors identify high-risk patients earlier and consider more aggressive treatments. The second study published in the International Journal of Cancer by the University of Oulu, Finland, analyzed 48 samples of cytogenetically normal acute myeloid leukemias. The study found that OGM detected clinically relevant structural variants in 46% of cases classified as normal by conventional karyotyping and the presence of OGM detected abnormalities was associated with worse survival in these individuals. The third study published in NPJ Precision Oncology by the Josep Carreras Leukemia Research Institute in Spain, studied subjects with therapy-related myeloid neoplasms and younger onset MDS.

It found that OGM produced a result in every sample, including all 8 where conventional banding failed and identified 134 additional genomic alterations. OGM defined genomic groups showed significant differences in overall survival with chromoanagenesis emerging as the strongest independent predictor of inferior overall survival. These publications join the T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia study we highlighted last quarter, also published in modern Pathology and conducted by researchers at MD Anderson and Johns Hopkins. Together, these publications, along with the 365 studies published year-to-date, give us confidence that the expanding body of clinical evidence is a leading indicator of future adoption and utilization of OGM. Turning to our fourth pillar. We continue to make progress on profitability.

In 2023, our adjusted gross margin was in the low 20% range. Since then, we've steadily improved it. And in the third quarter, we generated a gross margin of 48% compared with 46% in the same quarter last year. We've applied the same discipline to our cost structure. Operating expenses decreased 12% year-over-year to $10.5 million and adjusted operating expenses decreased 9% to $8.8 million. As revenue grows and our mix shifts towards higher-margin consumables and software, we expect these trends to carry us towards an adjusted EBITDA neutrality by the end of 2027.

So I'll turn the call over right now to Mark Adamchak, our Chief Accounting Officer, to review our Q3 2026 financial highlights and discuss our expectations for Q4 and the full year of 2026. Mark?

Mark Adamchak: Thanks, Al. Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $8.3 million, up 12% compared to Q3 2025. We sold 9,870 nanochannel array flow cells, up 18% compared to Q3 2025. We've been continuously investing in production and throughput. And as we reach the end of the year, we expect these constraints to ease. Turning to profitability. Adjusted gross margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 48% compared to 46% in Q3 2025. Third quarter 2026 adjusted operating expense was $8.8 million compared to $9.7 million in Q3 2025. We ended the quarter with $8.7 million in cash, cash equivalents and available-for-sale securities, including $0.5 million subject to certain restrictions. Turning to guidance.

For the full year 2026, we are reiterating our revenue guidance of $31 million to $33 million, representing growth of 9% to 16% over 2025. Within that range, we expect to land near the midpoint. We are encouraged by the momentum across our business and excited for the path ahead of Bionano. With that, I will turn the call back to the operator. Stephanie?

Operator: [Operator Instructions]. Our first question comes from Yi Chen of H.C. Wainwright.

Unknown Analyst: This is [indiscernible] for Yi. Looking at the September framework of $50 million to $54 million in 2027 revenue and approximately breakeven adjusted EBITDA exiting Q4, does that remain in your operating plan? What are the largest contributions to that acceleration from the current run rate? And what are supported by customer implementation schedules versus like milestones still ahead?

Albert Luderer: Yes. Thanks for the question. So our main focus for '27 is going to be to bring this company to EBITDA neutral, so that we can move into 2028 in a highly profitable mode. That is our main focus. Driving that is going to be our controlled expenses and also very rapid top line growth. So in September, when I spoke at the Wainwright conference, I presented a vision of what we might be in the future. And I want this to be a guideline for where this company and its underlying technology can be and what it can do as it transforms medicine.

So there are some large customers that are starting to come online for us, and they will be part of the majority of our growth as well as some of the supply constraints that Mark had mentioned in our production, which has really kept us from meeting a very strong customer demand this year.

Unknown Analyst: If I could follow on real quick. For the supply constraints, can you elaborate a little bit more on what remains to meet that time line once the backlog is cleared, will current capacity support the flow cells for your 2027 plan?

Albert Luderer: Yes. Yes, there's a long lead time for some of our most critical components and notably the silicon wafer that has all the nano channels. So yes, we've taken special effort to build up that supply and be able to essentially double our capacity that we have today. And we'll do that about halfway through midyear next year that will more than meet the capacity for '27 that we're projecting and also most of '28. So we think we have that in good shape, and we think we'll be essentially free and clear of any back orders by the end of this year. That's our plan right now.

Operator: Our next question is from Michael Okunewitch from Maxim Group.

Michael Okunewitch: Congrats on the progress. You posted some quite strong growth in terms of the flow cell utilization. So I wanted to see if you could talk a little bit about what the main drivers are for that particular increase? And if that is at all tempered by some of those supply constraints that you're facing.

Albert Luderer: Glad to expand on that, Michael, and thanks for the question. What we all believe right now is the -- first of all, the very strong clinical evidence that's global in nature, backed up by the CPT coding and now MolDX is favorable determination for hematologic oncology. We think that's a large driver of this. And we have several sites that have become major users, and we see some that are in queue to become also as large as some centers that we have. And I think it's mostly due to the fact they can offer the service and have a very good shot at getting paid for their services. So I think that's a huge part of it, Michael.

Michael Okunewitch: Appreciate that. And then also I wanted to congratulate you on the news with Sloan, a particularly exciting stuff. And I want to see if you could talk just a little bit about how Memorial Sloan Kettering plans to implement OGM through Bionano labs. Is this a pilot program? Or are they implementing it more broadly into their routine workflows?

Albert Luderer: That's a great question, and I'm really not prepared to answer that, but we can get back to you on that. So I think they received authorization to offer the service back right around the Wainwright conference time, early September. So as all these things, it takes a while to get going and then integrate into the clinical service and have the ordering physicians start to get used to and understand this new type of information that they are now privileged to see on these patients. So we've seen that adoption take a little bit of time, but at Sloan Kettering, I don't think it will take very long.

Michael Okunewitch: And one last one for me before I hop into the queue. I want to see if you could just provide a bit more color on what the customer profile looks like for Bionano labs versus actual internal adoption of OGM through a machine.

Albert Luderer: Well, our Bionano lab is -- it really exists to help us understand how our customers are experiencing our products. And while we do offer a commercial offering in the muscular dystrophy, we currently don't have any hematologic product, but that is part of our forward planning process that we're considering. So it's really -- that laboratory functions really as an in-house experience so that we can have real-time experiences that our customers have, which we can't always get.

Michael Okunewitch: All right. I appreciate your additional clarity and once again, congrats on all the progress.

Operator: Thank you. This does conclude the question-and-answer session for today. We thank you for your participation in today's conference, and this does conclude the program. You may now disconnect.

Prediction markets are booming, but that doesn’t make them a sound investment strategy.

The investing information provided on this page is for educational purposes only. NerdWallet, Inc. does not offer advisory or brokerage services, nor does it recommend or advise investors to buy or sell particular stocks, securities or other investments.

Around this time every year, we conduct NerdWallet’s annual broker review process. We assess what’s changed in the industry, discuss which brokerage features matter most (and which ones now matter less), and finally, we do the work by opening accounts to test them.

Prediction markets, which have made their way into some of the most popular investing apps, came up more than we expected in testing this year.

At first, we decided to simply collect information on who does and doesn’t offer access to them, without intending to reward or penalize a broker either way. It would be a neutral presentation of facts, not something that would factor into how we scored a broker.

But one afternoon, all together in the office, we confronted an uncomfortable question: “Do prediction markets, and such easy access to them within an investment app, go against NerdWallet’s editorial house views?”

After careful consideration, we all agreed: they do.

So we started to configure our 2027 rubric with a firmer stance against this trendy feature, penalizing brokers that actively market sports and entertainment event contracts, and whose prediction markets come with few, if any, guardrails.

We’ve distilled our discussion down to three main points:

These products are being marketed alongside investments.

We fear they could be discouraging long-term investing.

Let’s start here: Many aspects of trading could be seen as gambling-adjacent. Options, futures, highly leveraged single-day equity bets and even crypto can all easily fall into the “highly speculative” category. So why are we picking on prediction markets in particular?

In our view, a key differentiator is a much lower barrier to entry with few in-app guardrails in place.

Most of the products we mentioned above require some level of fluency — and at times even permission from the broker — to dabble in. To trade options, for example, you need to answer questions about your investing proficiency, your finances and more. And even after approval, the terminology required to trade can be so intimidating that the language itself can become an indirect deterrent.

Event contracts, which form the backbone of prediction markets, are largely presented in the vernacular, and our testing showed approval to trade them is completed with a few taps from the home screen. Moreover, their content is often unrelated to finance — according to a May 2026 report by the Pew Research Center, around 80% of volume on the prediction market platform Kalshi was for sports events[1]Pew Research Center. Trading Volume on Prediction Markets Has Soared in Recent Months. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Answering a binary question (yes/no; this/that), posed in everyday language about a familiar topic — something like, “Will the Knicks beat the Spurs on Sunday?” — can be far less daunting than figuring out what an options chain is or understanding forex pairs.

In other words, what makes prediction markets accessible to a wider audience is also what makes them problematic, especially when housed within an investing account. Which brings us to our next point.

On the platforms that feature them, we found that prediction markets almost always appear alongside stock and ETF trading. We think this is a mistake. What has made these mobile-first investing apps so good for so long (making it easy to move, manage and invest money through a beautiful interface) is what’s now making us nervous.

For example, most investing platforms let users do any number of smart things with idle cash. They could open an Individual Retirement Account (IRA), a custodial account or a robo-managed portfolio all through a single app. But now, they can dip into that same pot of money to bet on whether Beyoncé or Alicia Keys will play the Super Bowl halftime show.

But is anyone actually trading these event contracts? Let’s use data from publicly traded brokers that offer prediction markets to explore this.

In Q3 2026, Robinhood’s revenue from event contracts rose more than 600% year over year to $173 million, while the number of event contracts traded grew more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion[2]Robinhood. Robinhood Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . This was the second-highest source of transaction revenue behind options trading. In a forecast reported on by Cointelegraph, Bernstein analysts projected Robinhood’s prediction markets could drive $1.7 billion in annual revenue by 2028[3]Yahoo Finance. Bernstein Sees Robinhood Prediction Markets Reaching $1.7 Billion in Revenue by 2028, Topping Crypto. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Coinbase's Q1 2026 quarterly report called prediction markets “one of its fastest-scaling products ever, driven by strong retail interest[4]Coinbase. Coinbase Q1 Financial Results Show Resilient Financial Performance Driven by New All-Time High Crypto Trading Volume Market Share. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources ."

In a call discussing Webull’s Q2 results, U.S. CEO Anthony Denier noted trading volume in Webull’s nascent prediction market product grew about 70% quarter over quarter[5]Gloom. Webull (BULL) Q2 2026 earnings call transcript. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

Gemini’s Q2 report shows prediction market volume rose 93% quarter over quarter[6]Gemini. Shareholder Update Q2 2026. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

So, now that we’ve established that these markets are growing in popularity — and investing platforms appear to have a large incentive to lean into them — how are all those event contract traders faring? That brings us to our final point.

Is all this even worth it? Several studies show how hard it is to actually turn a profit in prediction markets. Here are a few:

One study, conducted by researchers at ESSEC Business School, HEC Montréal and the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management, covered 2.4 million Polymarket accounts across $67 billion in trading volume between November 2022 and March 2026, and found that 69% of users lost money[7]SSRN. Who Wins and Who Loses In Prediction Markets? Evidence from Polymarket. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . Moreover, the top 1% of users who made a profit accounted for about 76% of all gains. Translation: Even if you did turn a profit, there’s a good chance you didn’t make much.

A Bloomberg analysis supports this: From January 2025 to April 2026, more than 100,000 Polymarket accounts lost at least $1,000[8]Bloomberg. Most Prediction Market Traders Are Losing Money While Bots Rack Up Gains. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources . Of the 2 million active wallets studied, almost half made or lost less than $10 during the period, while far fewer accounts collected larger profits.

A separate Wall Street Journal analysis echoed the same trend: 67% of Polymarket profits go to 0.1% of accounts, and more than 70% of Polymarket users lost money[9]The Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

While there is far less data available on Kalshi trades (Polymarket runs on a public blockchain, making it easy to extract and analyze data), a Kalshi spokesperson confirmed in the Wall Street Journal analysis above that one month of data in 2026 showed there were 2.9 unprofitable users to each profitable user[10]Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 10, 2026. View all sources .

The first study above discusses how event contract trading is binary and zero-sum: If one trader wins, another loses. This means traders allocating money to these instruments could be missing out on aspects of equity markets that have helped create long-term wealth for previous generations.

“Unlike equity markets, there is no equity premium, no dividends, and no passive investment options. Their short maturities naturally encourage short-horizon trading, which is precisely what the behavioral finance literature has suggested is most destructive to wealth accumulation. Given the rapid growth of these platforms and their role as a potential entry point for young investors, understanding who bears the losses has direct implications for investor welfare and market regulation.”

As a reminder, the vast majority of Polymarket users bore the losses.

At NerdWallet, our mission has always been to help people make smarter financial decisions, so we’re sticking by that. Starting with our 2027 ratings, brokers that offer easy access to sports and entertainment event contracts will lose points in our scoring system because we believe this new product has the potential to harm long-term wealth building and doesn’t belong in investing platforms.

So, what’s a better way forward? Bring back the friction and make prediction markets a separate app. Financial institutions, businesses and individuals can still explore legitimate use cases for prediction markets, such as forecasting and hedging. And we’re not here to stop anyone from trading event contracts for entertainment with extra money. We just don’t want these markets so easily conflated with the legitimate investing vehicles these apps already offer. And our reviews will reflect that.

I do not think that is necessarily going to be the case for us now. I think we have faced most of that getting to where we are at today, as evidenced by this quarter. But I do think industry-wise, that is a bit of what will happen. However, overall, stocks need to be replenished. There is a rearmament going of an entire category of military strategy, tactics, weapons, mass low cost, mass precision. The cat is out of the bag. All of that is going to have to continue to happen. Historically, we have not seen Democrats spend less money on defense overall than the Republicans. I think in the big picture, the answer is no.

Is there going to be some short-term pain and some news media around how things are getting cut back or maybe that. Yeah, possibly, for sure. But every nation in the world right now is rearming, right, and retooling. So, we have got a 10-year policy cycle here of increased budgets. So, next question I have is, I have not seen contracts being announced for Orca. Do we expect any to come? Absolutely. Yeah, the product itself has been an incredible addition to the product line. It has opened up an entire new set of doors for us.

It has also given great capability to our existing product line, because remember, most buying is happening not for a single purpose, but for missions now. Being able to combine fixed-wing capability, long-range strike, long-range loiter, or long-time loiter capabilities along with the multi-rotor line has been fantastic. So the answer is, I cannot say more than that, but the answer is yeah, super excited what was happening there, and I think you will be pleased over the next couple of quarters. Are we still focused on counter-drone technology? For sure. So we were awarded a DEVCOM contract to develop a mobile counter-drone capability. That thing is moving along quite nicely.

There are already demonstrations happening in various different aspects of the DOW. We are continuing to push forward and invest in that particular area. We have been participating in bids and opportunities around counter-drone, in particular on our public safety, around security and private security. We really believe we built up a very significant pipeline of work in that regard, as well as what we are doing in public safety and on the military side. So counter-drones, it is just becoming part of what a drone company is. It is pretty tough to be doing drones at all unless you are also doing counter-drone.

So they are being one and the same has given us great advantage, and it is a lot of the same expertise, a lot of the same equipment, a lot of the same policy, so not a huge amount of cost to making sure that you can offer 100% solution to your customer. Then, final question here is, what is management's long-term and mid-term plan to achieve self-sustaining cash flow without relying on continued share dilution? Well, we are going to be driving three areas. So maybe just to recap. We have three particular verticals that we focus on. We have our commercial industrial, which historically was quite prevalent for us. Now it is our smallest division, but really important.

We do a specific type of work in there that is key, especially for the future. We have our public safety business, and we have our military business. Currently, the military business is driving things forward. We have Canadian military, we have U.S. military, and we have international military, much of which we will be talking quite a bit about over the next couple of weeks. It is really about just building size, volume in those areas now. We have developed incredible, I believe anyway, incredible capabilities in those areas that match what those particular militaries are looking for, and it has taken them those years, those militaries, to understand what it is that they really need.

We will be providing products into them, but also providing manufacturing capability. More of that to come in the coming weeks. On the public safety side, we are dealing primarily in Canada and the United States. We are just about to launch our DFR product, which we are excited about. Our campus facility, our campus program in particular, has really taken off for us. We are engaged only with three campuses right now by design, very simply because we are really working through all the very finite details of operations and training and such. We literally have a list of 1,500 campuses that have inquired right now. There are 3,000 in the United States in total.

We will go full bore on that after the next quarter, and we get through the rest of the implementation of these three so that we have got showcases, testimonies, use case scenarios, studies, and every question that can be answered around that. Also in public safety, we tend to focus on small, rural, tribal, sheriff, and border, because our equipment is really designed a bit more for heavier use, a longer range, heavier payloads, multi-payloads, things like that. It lends itself more to those types of environments, as opposed to being necessarily in New York or San Francisco or such, where we have got great competitors like Skydio and BRINC that are battling it out for market share there.

Then obviously on the military side, we are going to grow with the military budgets as they grow over the next number of years. Now listen, we also think we have got a terrific lineup of products that are differentiated, and we will continue to hone in and make those differences, continue to use our ITS team, our Integrated Tactical Solutions team, to embed with our customers and learn what is the things that they need the most, what are the nuances that make our equipment better use for them, and we will just continue to do more of the same.

On that, it takes a lot when you are building a company that has seven product lines to serve that type of a customer base. You kind of have to go wide first before you go deep. Now, that is against conventional startup wisdom. We're in a unique situation where we're a 27-year-old startup. We had the ability to go wide before we went deep, and so that breadth now is pretty much put in place. I think what you'll see actually over the very short order here, but certainly over the coming quarters, you'll see the depth of that now be able to penetrate and start to drive some pretty significant announcements and orders for us.

On that note, I think I've covered off everything. I appreciate everybody's patience. I really wanted to thank three particular groups. First of all, the people that work with us, our employees, the amount of commitment that we see in this organization, what people are willing to do to live our purpose, which is to be of service to others, and to save time, money, and lives. First of all, thank you to you. Thanks also to our customers, for sure, for the amount of feedback and input that you've been giving us, how deeply you're working with us, and how you have a long-term view of what your business can become because of what we can bring to you.

It inspires us. Obviously to our shareholders, thanks for your patience. This has taken a lot longer than we all thought. It has for the entire industry, but we couldn't be where we are at today without you. Man, we are excited about where we're at and what we'll see coming out in the very, very near future here. From all of us to all you, we really appreciate it, and we'll continue to do our best to be of service. Thanks very much, and talk to you soon.

Early aerospace deliveries arrived, but a $1.8 million inventory write-down hit gross results.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Factorial Energy Inc. (FAC -4.70%) transitioned to a commercial-stage company in the third quarter of 2026, recording its first revenue from solid-state battery cell deliveries to the aerospace market. Management reported reaching an energy density of 450 watt-hours per kilogram for its aerospace cells, meeting its year-end performance target ahead of schedule while achieving a pilot line yield of 85%. The company is executing a fabless business model, forming strategic partnerships with manufacturers like SK On to leverage existing global production capacity for the automotive sector. Factorial revised its full-year spending and capital expenditure guidance downward, citing cost reclassifications and disciplined operational management as it prepares for meaningful revenue growth in 2027.

So that is why we think that for this technology, it will be able to get to the energy density much more quickly because lithium metal is literally the lightest metal on Earth right now. And at the same time, you can push for high power. Without the traditional physical limits. That the lithium ion battery are having.

If you grab the top 5 automakers, they probably 50% of the market already.

Mortgage rates are a little lower today. It probably won't last, thanks to new inflation data that has investors even more confident that the Federal Reserve will hike rates next month. You can read more on that below the charts.

Today, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 6.9% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is eight basis points lower than yesterday and 17 basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

This morning the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) dropped the October Consumer Price Index, which shows that inflation rose another 0.4% last month. This outpaced expectations: Economists had forecasted an increase of 0.3%. CPI is one of two key measures of inflation, which the Federal Reserve aims to keep in check relative to the strength of the labor market. (The Fed looks more closely at a different inflation measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures Index, which comes out Nov. 25.)

Raising the federal funds rate is the Fed’s main tool for bringing inflation down, and futures traders are banking on a rate hike when the committee meets Dec. 8-9. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates directly, but an anticipated rate hike can put upward pressure on mortgage rates, which respond to investors’ expectations for the economy and Fed policy.

Central bankers raised the federal funds rate in September, but it hasn’t been enough to pull inflation closer to the Fed’s target of 2%. Investors aren’t sure that one more hike in December will do the trick, either. According to CME FedWatch, further rate hikes may be in store for January.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.4% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

#3048. Rocket Lab: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Electron's 96% mission success rate across nearly 100 flights gives customers a track record to lean on before committing to Neutron's premium pricing.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 9, 2026, Rocket Lab (RKLB +6.54%) reported quarterly revenue of $268 million, representing 73% year-over-year growth. Global launch supply remains constrained, so spacecraft builders with proven flight hardware can command higher prices. Scaling flight cadence and software capabilities expands the company's addressable market. Three key takeaways from management stand out for long-term investors.

Global launch availability remains tight, so rocket providers can raise launch fees rather than offer early customer discounts. For Neutron, its new medium-lift launch vehicle designed to carry 13 tonnes, customer demand pushed base contract prices higher as early flight slots filled up into the next decade.

Execution consistency matters for satellite operators who can't afford payload delays. Rocket Lab manufactures the Electron, its small orbital launch vehicle, at a rapid pace while maintaining a 96% mission success rate across nearly 100 flights, helping it retain commercial and defense customers.

Expanding beyond launch into constellation management provides predictable recurring revenue. Rocket Lab completed a $2.4 billion at-the-market equity offering program, in which it sells shares in the open market over time.

Launch capacity constraints and satellite constellation build-outs continue to surge, driving factory floors to full operational capacity. In its Space Systems segment, which designs and builds satellites and components, Rocket Lab maintains an operational footprint spanning solar cells, flight software, and satellite subassemblies. Vertically integrated manufacturing shields the company from broader supply chain bottlenecks. Meanwhile, growing backlog, which represents signed customer contracts awaiting delivery, provides long-term revenue visibility while management focuses on launch cadence execution and cost discipline.

Building reusable rocket infrastructure requires substantial early capital investments, but established operational momentum positions the company to capture expanding market share across commercial and national security missions.

#3042. Car Insurance Soars for Drivers With Poor Credit; Here’s What to Do

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

While building your credit, shop around for auto insurance quotes. Some insurers are more lenient than others.

Lead Writer & Licensed Insurance Specialist

Your driving record may be spotless, but if you have poor credit, car insurance companies view you as a risk — and they’re significantly raising your rates.

Over the past three years, drivers with poor credit have seen auto insurance premiums surge 37.7%, according to NerdWallet’s 2026 Auto Insurance Rates Report. These price hikes were even steeper than those faced by drivers with good credit who caused a crash or got a DUI.

In January 2023, someone with poor credit and a clean driving record would pay a median of $2,864 per year for full-coverage car insurance, NerdWallet’s analysis found. By January 2026, premiums for this driver had risen to $3,944 — an increase of $1,081 per year. By comparison, the same driver with good credit saw an increase of only $576.

“Credit scores are one of the most harmful things that results in you paying higher auto insurance premiums,” says Michael DeLong, a research and advocacy associate with the Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit Consumer Federation of America. “The penalties are extremely severe.”

While higher premiums after a wreck or DUI may not be a surprise, DeLong says many drivers aren’t aware their credit scores will affect their car insurance rates. To further complicate things, building credit can take months.

But there are ways to get relief more quickly. DeLong suggests comparing car insurance quotes from multiple companies, because some insurers penalize poor credit less than others. Raising your deductible, evaluating your coverage and avoiding small claims can also help.

NerdWallet’s analysis found that insurers raised rates more sharply from 2023 to 2026 for drivers with poor credit than for those with good credit — even if the poor-credit driver had a flawless record while the good-credit driver had a DUI, speeding ticket or at-fault crash.

When our sample driver with poor credit also had a recent DUI or speeding ticket, rate increases were even greater. Prices for a full-coverage policy went up by more than 40% for drivers with poor credit and a recent DUI, the biggest increase of any profile we analyzed.

Drivers often think it’s unfair for credit to affect car insurance prices, DeLong says, since it isn’t directly linked to driving behavior. Some states agree; California, Hawaii and Massachusetts don’t allow credit as a factor in setting auto insurance rates.

However, insurers say credit scores can indicate the likelihood that a driver will file a claim.[1]National Association of Insurance Commissioners. Credit-Based Insurance Scores. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources They use what’s called a credit-based insurance score — similar to the typical credit scores used by lenders but weighted differently.

“It helps in predicting expected claims activity and loss costs more accurately,” said Norman Niami, a member of the American Academy of Actuaries' Automobile Insurance Committee, in an email.

The practice has been controversial, with critics arguing it disproportionately hurts low-income and minority drivers. But a Federal Trade Commission report to Congress in July 2007 concluded that credit-based insurance scores were strong predictors of risk even when controlled for income, race and ethnicity.[2]A Report to Congress by the Federal Trade Commission. Credit-Based Insurance Scores: Impacts on Consumers of Automobile Insurance. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources

The explanation may be that some people simply tend to take risks, according to a statistical analysis published in the North American Actuarial Journal in 2016.[3]North American Actuarial Journal. Empirical Evidence on the Use of Credit Scoring for Predicting Insurance Losses with Psycho-social and Biochemical Explanations. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources Researchers concluded that risk-taking behavior can affect credit scores as well as insurance claims. Their analysis found that average losses per policy were 64.6% higher for drivers with the lowest credit scores than for those with the best credit.

Working to build your credit over time may help lower your car insurance premiums, but it’s not a sure thing. A credit-based insurance score is just one of many factors (along with things like location, age and driving history) that insurers use to rate a person’s risk.

Building credit “can produce a noticeable premium decrease in some cases, while producing little or no change in others,” Niami said, depending on whether the new score causes an insurer to move you into a better rating tier. Each insurer sets its own score thresholds, so a score viewed as “poor” by one insurer might be considered “fair” by another.

At the same time, consumer advocates argue it’s difficult for many people to take the steps needed to strengthen their credit scores.

“Most people probably have some idea that you can improve your credit score by trying to pay your bills regularly and reliably, and using different kinds of financial resources and credit cards,” DeLong says.

“But again, that’s easier said than done," he says. "If you’re struggling at a low-wage job and trying to juggle bills, or if you don’t easily have access to a credit card, that advice may not be especially helpful."

Drivers with poor credit or no credit may be able to take other steps to lower their premiums.

Comparing car insurance quotes from different companies is one of the best ways to ensure you have the cheapest rate possible. Insurers set their own pricing formulas, and some are more forgiving of poor credit than others. A NerdWallet analysis of October 2026 rates found that in about half (49.3%) of U.S. ZIP codes in states that allow credit scoring, the cheapest insurer for a driver with poor credit was a different company than the cheapest for a driver with good credit.

Although you can’t improve your risk profile overnight, “there’s a bunch of small things you can do that over a two- to three-year span make you look a lot better” to insurers, says Bradley Flowers, founder of Portal Insurance agency in Mobile, Alabama.

Consider a higher deductible. Raising your car insurance deductible — the amount of a future claim that you agree to cover yourself — lowers your premium and signals to insurers that you’re less likely to file a claim. But be sure you can afford to pay the higher deductible if you have to make a claim.

Adjust how you’re billed by insurers. By signing up for automatic payments and ensuring you don’t miss insurance payments each month, you’ll get a small discount while improving your risk profile for insurers.

Avoid minor claims if you can. Flowers recommends thinking twice about filing minor claims, such as windshield cracks. “When you’re in one of these situations, let’s save our insurance for the really bad stuff,” he suggests.

Lastly, be sure your coverage fits your vehicle. If you could afford to replace your car on your own, consider dropping collision and comprehensive coverage to bring your premiums down. Your trimmed-down policy would still provide you with liability coverage after a crash, while leaving you to cover damage to your vehicle.

NerdWallet's 2026 Auto Insurance Rates Report is based on an analysis of more than 1.4 billion rate estimates provided by Quadrant Information Services for all 50 states and Washington, D.C., from January 2023 to January 2026.

Quadrant derives its rate data from modeled estimates based on carrier rating algorithms; figures do not reflect every available carrier or every consumer's individual rate. Liberty Mutual does not participate in Quadrant's rate data and is not represented in this analysis.

Quadrant’s figures are modeled rate estimates produced by running a fixed driver profile through carrier rating algorithms. They represent both new business and renewal rate estimates, and they are not a record of what actual drivers paid.

NerdWallet anchored its analysis to a 3-year old Toyota Camry LE, ensuring each analysis period reflected rates for the same-aged car.

The primary rate analysis is based on a 35-year-old single driver with good credit, no recent at-fault accidents or driving violations, and a full-coverage policy with $1,000 deductibles for collision and comprehensive coverage. Rates are pooled across male and female drivers.

In states where drivers must carry other types of insurance not included in our full coverage profile specifications, we added the minimum amount of coverage required by those states. Some policies include additional coverage at the insurer’s discretion.

In addition to our base profile driver with good credit and a spotless driving history, we analyzed rates for the following driver profiles:

Drivers with an at-fault crash. We added a single at-fault crash causing $10,000 in property damage.

Drivers with a speeding ticket. We added a single speeding ticket for driving 16 mph over the speed limit.

Drivers with a DUI. We added a single drunken-driving violation.

Drivers with poor credit. This is the same as our regular base profile, except the driver has poor credit instead of good credit. We also analyzed rates for drivers with poor credit and each of the three incidents above.

NerdWallet applied a strict comparability filter before calculating year-over-year figures. Only coverage variants and carrier/state combinations present in all four years of data were included in median calculations. This ensures reported changes reflect genuine pricing shifts among stable carriers, rather than differences caused by insurers entering markets, exiting, or going insolvent during the analysis period.

#3039. TransDigm: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Its decentralized bolt-on model lets TransDigm grow without betting the company on oversized deals.

On its fourth quarter of 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, TransDigm (TDG +0.55%) announced fiscal 2027 revenue guidance with a midpoint of $12.05 billion. That top-line target reflects double-digit expansion across key aerospace markets, offering long-term investors a clear look at how disciplined capital deployment drives earnings. Three things management said stand out.

TransDigm relies on its 57 operating units to identify and integrate small acquisitions, known as bolt-ons, rather than depending solely on central dealmakers. This decentralized approach expands the acquisition pipeline without forcing the company into risky, oversized deals.

Temporary dips in passenger travel don't crush demand for replacement parts because airlines must keep existing fleets operational. TransDigm expects commercial aftermarket revenue to recover to baseline levels whenever short-term travel disruptions end.

New military repair regulations pose little threat because TransDigm self-funds product development and holds proprietary intellectual property (IP) rights. Direct sales to the government account for roughly 6% of revenue, and less than 1% involves repairable parts.

Factory automation drives margin expansion as original equipment manufacturer (OEM) production climbs. TransDigm focuses capital expenditures (capex) on efficiency gains while tracking factory productivity to preserve operational leverage.

Proprietary aerospace parts provide structural moats that generate durable cash flow. Management monitors capital allocation opportunities and maintains substantial liquidity to deploy when attractive acquisitions emerge.
